TI Identification of Differences in Eye Movements in Early Readers with
   Good & Bad Reading Comprehension
SO INVESTIGACIONES SOBRE LECTURA
LA English
DT Article
DE Reading comprehension; Eye-tracking; Sentence reading; Literacy;
   Vocabulary
ID MECHANISMS; CHILDREN; ABILITY
AB Reading comprehension is a core, cross-curricular skill essential for both academic and personal contexts, preparing students for future challenges. International reports indicate a need to improve reading comprehension, but do not identify the possible causes of underperformance. One way to analyse these difficulties is through eye movements during reading. This research aims to explore whether there are differences in eye movement patterns between students with bad and good reading comprehension scores, providing a detailed comparative characterisation of reading processing according to comprehension level. A total of 106 students were assessed using a pre-test of reading comprehension (PROLEC-R), classifying students into those with low and high reading comprehension. A sample of 56 students (31 with high scores and 25 with low scores) was selected for the analysis of eye movements and vocabulary. The results indicate differences in eye movement patterns between the two groups, reflecting how real-time processing varies according to performance. They show that bad readers have a higher number of fixations and saccades, taking longer to make regressions, are slower at rereading, and take longer to identify and access the meaning of words, with a significantly smaller vocabulary. No such trend is observed in saccade amplitude and pupil diameter. These findings have significant implications for understanding difficulties in reading comprehension and contribute to improving strategies for early detection and educational intervention in reading comprehension.

TI Reading competence and linguistic creativity in secondary education. A
   cross-sectional study
SO INVESTIGACIONES SOBRE LECTURA
LA English
DT Article
DE Secondary education; reading competence; creativity; linguistic
   creativity; cognitive development
ID COGNITIVE-ABILITIES; COMPREHENSION; CHILDREN
AB Reading competence and creative thinking are considered fundamental competencies in contemporary education, and their assessment provides critical insight into the efficacy of educational systems. Accordingly, the aim of this study is to conduct a cross-sectional analysis of the development of reading competence and linguistic creativity among 524 Spanish secondary school students and to explore the relationship between these two competencies. This descriptive study utilizes validated instruments to assess reading competence, creative potential (defined as problem-finding ability), and linguistic creativity (measured as the ability to generate both conventional and novel metaphors). Results indicate that while reading proficiency and conventional metaphor production exhibit steady growth throughout secondary education, the production of novel metaphors and general creative potential remain stable. Female students obtained significantly higher scores than their male peers across all variables, except for creative potential. Furthermore, reading competence was found to correlate with both measures of linguistic creativity. These findings suggest that current teaching practices successfully foster basic literacy but fail to stimulate the higher-order executive processes required for creative thinking, underscoring the need for instructional changes discussed herein.

TI LecDis-S Test: Diagnostic Assessment for Reading in Academic Disciplines
   within the Health Sector
SO INVESTIGACIONES SOBRE LECTURA
LA English
DT Article
DE Academic literacy; higher education; subject-specific reading;
   diagnostic tests; academic texts
AB As an educational process specific to higher education, academic literacy benefits from the use of an appropriate diagnostic tool, as this enables the level of students' communication skills to be identified at the start of the teaching and learning process. This article presents the design, development, implementation and analysis of the results of an original diagnostic tool called LecDis-S (short for "disciplinary reading in health"), which aimed to assess the reading proficiency of health degree students entering a Chilean university using stimulus texts relating to human anatomy. Quantitative analysis yielded the following results: the assessed population had difficulty correctly answering questions relating to literal reading (textual dimension), particularly those concerning sentence comprehension. In contrast, the pragmatic and critical dimensions (assessing factors such as the context of text circulation and the speaker's stance) demonstrated a higher level of achievement, despite the instrument's high overall difficulty. This evaluation allows us to conclude that LecDis-S constitutes a preliminary diagnostic test of academic disciplinary reading competence in first-year health students. However, the overall internal consistency of the total score was modest, so the instrument should not be presented as fully validated or used to inform high-stakes individual decisions. In its current state, its main utility is to support group assessments and identify areas of reading difficulty at the start of training, particularly given that it is constructed using authentic texts from a specific discipline.

SO INVESTIGACIONES SOBRE LECTURA
LA English

AB The way we consume information today is characterised by speed, fragmentation and dispersion. These dynamics are reinforced by social media platforms such as TikTok and Instagram, which have established habits based on immediacy and short-form content. In this context, more selective and superficial forms of reading are favoured, particularly in digital environments, where the absence of metacognitive strategies can hinder sustained attention, reflection and deep understanding. International frameworks such as PISA, PIRLS and PIAAC, as well as the European Union's key competences, recognise the cross-curricular nature of reading and its importance for learning, social participation and everyday life. The results show significant differences in favour of the intervention groups, particularly among those using EduLeo most frequently, highlighting the importance of regular reading skills training.

AB The OECD's PISA report evaluates, among other competencies, the reading performance of teenagers globally, including Spain, in which representative scores are obtained from all autonomous communities. This study focuses on analysing the relationship between the COVID-19 lockdown and the reading literacy of students in the Canary Islands in PISA 2022, while also considering factors such as parental education level and student gender. Furthermore, boys consistently performed worse than girls. Educational policy should prioritise targeted support for students from less advantaged backgrounds to mitigate the inequalities identified

TI Literary education in the classroom through the recovery of myths in
   Mexican children's theatre. An analysis of perceptions
SO INVESTIGACIONES SOBRE LECTURA
LA English
DT Article
DE Education; didactics; classroom; theatre; cultural identity
ID TOOL
AB The aim of this study is to analyse children's and young people's perceived self-efficacy in relation to concepts associated with the pedagogical recovery of pre-Hispanic myths through theatre in the classroom. Adopting a mixed-methods descriptive approach, statistical analyses are used through the implementation of a mixed questionnaire administered to 207 students from a school in the State of Puebla (Mexico). The internal consistency of the instruments implemented (alpha = 0.837) supports its reliability as an analytical tool. To confirm the adequacy of the data, the Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin measure of sampling adequacy (0.70), was calculated and confirmed by Bartlett's test of sphericity (chi 2 (37) = 337.72; p < 0.05). The results reveal students' limited self-perceived ability to recognise and define certain foundational Mexican myths and confirm the need to reflect on the construction of identity through self-discovery and the discovery of otherness. This process is fostered through the linguistic and literary learning of myths implemented in the classroom through theatre, which is regarded as an essential pedagogical tool in students' holistic development.

TI Teachers and the Tech Ideology: Navigating Influence in Israeli Public
   Education
SO TEACHERS COLLEGE RECORD
LA English
DT Article
DE Teacher perspectives; tech ideology; neoliberalism; institutional
   isomorphism; educational aims
ID NEOCONSERVATISM; NEOLIBERALISM; POLITICS; SCHOOLS; END
AB Background: Technology and the tech industry have gained increasing power in many societies over the past half century. In Israel, like other countries in the Global North, the public education system has experienced a shift toward enterprise culture, with policymakers and educators jointly collaborating in idealizing the Israeli high-tech sector.Focus of the Study: In light of the growing dominance of tech ideology in the Israeli education system, the study explores how dominant views of the tech industry may influence teachers' perceptions of the industry and tech ideology's role in education. We were particularly interested in exploring how a host of factors, including teachers' previous professional experience in the tech industry (or lack thereof) and the content area they teach, shape their perspectives on the involvement of the tech industry in Israeli public education.Research Design: Our data consists of interviews with 22 Israeli high school teachers. The participants were purposively chosen to include two groups of teachers who differ in their professional experience and background: teachers who joined the profession following substantial experience in the tech industry and teachers who joined the teaching profession early on and evolved solely through its ranks.Conclusion: Findings suggest that (1) teachers both admire and resist tech ideology and its impact on schools, and (2) their attitudes toward the tech industry relate to their educational aims, highlighting the significance of tech involvement and its hegemonic impact on the future of teachers and public education. The discussion employs institutional isomorphism to illustrate how the education system might imitate the tech industry, identifying discursive and normative conditions under which institutional educational change may be legitimized or resisted.

AB Context: Coaching has been associated with changes in teacher practice and gains in student learning, but logistical and financial obstacles limit the extent to which individualized coaching can be offered and sustained. These challenges are especially pronounced in social studies, a subject area where teachers receive little content-specific oversight, professional development, or instructional coaching. TI Multicultural Teaching Self-Efficacy and Instructional Practices in
   Linguistically Diverse ELA Classrooms
SO TEACHERS COLLEGE RECORD
LA English
DT Article
DE Multicultural teaching self-efficacy; MTSE; instructional practices;
   instructional quality; linguistic diversity; multilingual education;
   multicultural education
ID LANGUAGE; STUDENT; QUALITY; MANAGEMENT
AB Background: As secondary English language arts (ELA) classrooms become increasingly linguistically diverse, concerns persist about teachers' preparedness to provide rigorous and equitable instruction in multilingual classrooms. Multicultural teaching self-efficacy (MTSE) has been associated with diversity-responsive teaching practices. However, little is known about how MTSE relates to instructional practices in linguistically diverse secondary ELA classrooms or whether these relationships vary across levels of linguistic diversity.Purpose: This study examines the relationship between secondary ELA teachers' MTSE and three dimensions of instructional practice: classroom management, instructional clarity, and cognitive activation. It also investigates whether these relationships vary according to the level of classroom linguistic diversity.Research Design: This study used data from the 2018 U.S. Teaching and Learning International Survey (TALIS), drawing on a nationally representative sample of 364 secondary ELA teachers. Survey-weighted multivariable regression analyses were conducted to examine associations between MTSE and instructional practices and to test whether classroom linguistic diversity moderated these relationships.Conclusions: MTSE was not directly associated with classroom management, instructional clarity, or cognitive activation. However, classroom linguistic diversity moderated several of these relationships. Teachers in multilingual classrooms reported lower levels of instructional clarity and cognitive activation overall, yet those with higher MTSE reported greater use of both practices. These findings highlight the importance of MTSE in sustaining rigorous and equitable instruction in linguistically diverse ELA classrooms.

TI "We Don't Need Everything from One Person": How Possibility Models and
   Anti-mentors Shape STEMM Doctoral Student Mentors' Pathways
SO TEACHERS COLLEGE RECORD
LA English
DT Article
DE mentoring; graduate education; socialization; possible selves;
   computing; narrative inquiry
ID SOCIALIZATION; IDENTITY; EXPERIENCES; KNOWLEDGE; EDUCATION; OUTCOMES;
   FUTURE; EQUITY; SKILLS
AB Background: Doctoral students' role as mentees is well documented in studies on faculty-student mentorship in science, technology, engineering, mathematics, and medicine (STEMM); however, they also frequently serve as mentors to earlier-stage (e.g., undergraduate) students. To date, studies have not yet substantively investigated how the mentoring support doctoral students receive from past and present mentors may motivate them to serve in a similar role.Research Questions: Focusing within the field of informatics, this qualitative study examined how past and present mentors shaped doctoral students' understanding of their possible pathways to and through doctoral education and their motivations to be mentors. We asked: (1) How do informatics doctoral students make meaning of their past and present mentors as possibility models or anti-mentors in their educational pathways?, and (2) What aspects of relationships with past and present possibility models or anti-mentors shape informatics doctoral students' motivations to become mentors?Research Design: Guided by the theoretical perspectives of graduate socialization and possible selves, we used a critical constructivist paradigm with narrative inquiry to make meaning of participants' past, present, and future development as mentors. The data for this study included adapted education journey maps and two semistructured 60- to 75-minute interviews with 10 informatics doctoral students, with each data source exploring how past and present mentors serve as possibility models or anti-mentors in doctoral students' trajectories as mentees and emerging mentors. We then applied a three-part analytic process to establish organizational, theoretical, and substantive categorizations and facilitate our (re)storying process of participants' narratives.Conclusions: We offer three overarching findings discussing how, as participants received mentorship and conceptualized their motivations to provide support as mentors, they reflected on: (1) clarifying mentoring philosophies and values, (2) redefining potential pathways as mentees and mentors, and (3) understanding stage-ahead mentoring as fundamental to doctoral student training. By positioning doctoral students as mentors rather than only mentees, this study advances our understanding of the roots and potential consequences of mentorship in doctoral education, thereby informing how the next generation of mentors is trained.

TI A Longitudinal QuantCrit Study of Disaggregated Community College
   Enrollment: How Economic and Institutional Contexts Shaped Open Access
   from 2017 to 2021
SO TEACHERS COLLEGE RECORD
LA English
DT Article
DE QuantCrit; community colleges; race; gender; labor markets; COVID-19;
   higher education policy
ID CHOICE; EDUCATION
AB Background: Community colleges are central access points to postsecondary education, particularly for racially minoritized, low-income, first-generation, and adult students. However, the COVID-19 pandemic intensified existing inequalities in health, employment, and educational access. Understanding how community college enrollment changed before and after the COVID-19 outbreak requires attention not only to aggregate trends but also to how institutional and labor market conditions shaped enrollment differently across race and gender.Purpose: This study examines how institutional and labor market conditions shaped first-time degree-seeking community college enrollment at the intersection of race and gender in the United States before and after the COVID-19 outbreak. The study centers the COVID-19 outbreak as a natural intervention that exposed how systemic inequities in health, employment security, and educational opportunity affected access to open-access community colleges.Research Design: Using national datasets from 2017 to 2021, this study applied a Quantitative Critical Race (QuantCrit) approach and a longitudinal multilevel mixed-effects design. The analysis focused on first-time degree-seeking enrollment in open-access community colleges, disaggregated by race and gender. Institutional characteristics, minority-serving institution status, and local labor market conditions were included as key predictors, with the COVID-19 period modeled as a critical disruption in enrollment patterns.Conclusions: The findings show that community college enrollment declines were sharpest for Black and Latina women, while enrollment patterns varied substantially across minority-serving colleges. Labor market conditions were also associated with racialized and gendered disparities: local unemployment was linked to higher White enrollment but lower enrollment for students of color, while growth in healthcare and social-service employment was associated with reduced enrollment for women of color. These findings suggest that institutional and economic contexts interact with racialized and gendered structures to shape who accesses higher education. The study calls for equity-centered policy approaches and more critical uses of quantitative data in postsecondary education research.

TI What drives teachers' self-efficacy in the digital age? Insights from
   online K-12 Chinese language education
SO PORTA LINGUARUM
LA English
DT Article
DE Teachers' self-efficacy; Language teachers; Influential factors; Online
   education; K-12 education
ID TEACHING CHINESE; RESPECT; CONTEXT
AB As online K-12 language teaching grows, teachers' self-efficacy is critical but its factors in digital settings remain unclear. This study addresses this gap by examining the self-efficacy levels and influencing factors among online K-12 Chinese as a Foreign Language (CFL) teachers. Using a mixed-methods approach with data from 610 questionnaires and 13 interviews, results indicated generally high teachers' self-efficacy. This study extends self-efficacy theory into the online CFL context and offers practical implications for digital pedagogy, platform design, and teacher training.

TI Impact of a virtual reality intervention on Palestinian EFL students'
   speaking skills
SO PORTA LINGUARUM
LA English
DT Article
DE virtual reality; speaking skills; English as a foreign language;
   situated learning theory; immersive learning
AB This study evaluated the effectiveness of a virtual reality (VR) application in improving English speaking skills among seventh-and eighth-grade female students at Ziad Abu Ein Primary Upper School in Palestine, based on Situated Learning Theory, which emphasises the effectiveness of contextualised learning through real-life simulations. The sample included 66 students, assigned to an experimental group (n = 43) using the VR and a control group (n = 23) studying via a traditional method. The application provided immersive environments through 360-degree videos and interactive activities linked to daily life. A Cambridge English A2 speaking test was administered pre-and post-intervention to measure outcomes. The experimental group showed significant improvement in four out of five indicators under study (grammar and vocabulary, pronunciation, interactive communication, and the total score) with medium to large effect sizes. Students across the three performance levels established in the study benefited similarly, reflecting equitable learning opportunities. Results indicated that the VR environment enhanced spoken production, an outcome particularly valuable in the resource-limited Palestinian context. The study recommends expanding this approach to other schools and age groups and evaluating the long-term effectiveness of VR in teaching English as a foreign language.

TI Pedagogical models of generative AI in Secondary English language
   teaching
SO PORTA LINGUARUM
LA English
DT Article
DE Generative artificial intelligence; English Language Teaching; Teaching
   practic-es; Secondary Education; Pedagogical innovation
AB The rapid rise of generative artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping the pedagogical landscape of English Language Teaching (ELT), particularly in secondary education where teachers confront heterogeneous proficiency levels, escalating curricular demands and evolving expectations for digitally mediated learning. While existing research has examined teacher attitudes, digital competence and ethical concerns, far less is known about the discipline-specific instructional practices through which English teachers operationalise AI within real classroom contexts. In addition, the study proposes a conceptual framework for interpreting emerging modes of AI-mediated English language teaching, situating these practices within contemporary debates on teacher agency, pedagogical design and technological mediation, and contributing to a more nuanced understanding of how AI is being negotiated within language education.

TI Continuous Professional Development and its effects on resilience and
   job satisfaction in L2 teaching staff
SO PORTA LINGUARUM
LA English
DT Article
DE EFL; teacher satisfaction; professional development; contextual factors;
   resilience
ID SCHOOL CONTEXT; SELF-EFFICACY; TEACHERS; CLIMATE; STRESS; SCALE;
   COLLABORATION; MOTIVATION
AB The present study examines the potential mediating role of participation in continuous professional development (CPD) activities in the relationship among contextual factors, resilience, and teacher job satisfaction, with job satisfaction conceptualized as the dependent variable. The participants consisted of 300 L2 teaching staff working in elementary schools, high schools, and universities. Four data collection instruments were employed. The first instrument was the Professional Development Scale (PDS), developed by de Vries et al. (2010), which includes three subdimensions: updating activities, reflective activities, and collaborative activities. The second instrument was the Perceived School Context Scale (PSCS), developed by Skaalvik and Skaalvik (2010), which measures contextual aspects such as time pressure, autonomy, discipline problems, and supervisory support. The third instrument was the Resilience Scale, developed by Connor and Davidson (2003). Finally, teacher job satisfaction was measured using the Teacher Satisfaction Scale developed by Ho and Au (2006). The findings indicate that resilience, education level, autonomy, educational background, and updating activities significantly predict participation in CPD, and that CPD activities mediate the relationship between resilience and teacher job satisfaction.

TI Artificial Intelligence in teaching creative writing: A systematic
   review in L1 and additional languages learning contexts
SO PORTA LINGUARUM
LA English
DT Article
DE Artificial Intelligence; Creative Writing; Language Learning; Large
   Language Models; Writing
AB The emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly generative models, has profoundly impacted language education, creating a research gap concerning its application in creative writing. This systematic review follows the PRISMA 2020 guidelines to analyse 21 experimental or quasi-experimental studies published between 2020 and 2025, exploring the use ofAI in teaching creative writing in both first language (L1) and additional language (AL) contexts. The findings show a nascent but rapidly expanding field, with 76% of included studies published in 2024 or 2025. Research is primarily conducted in higher education, and commercial Large Language Models (LLMs) like ChatGPT are the most frequently used tools. Creative writing tasks overwhelmingly centre on short stories, particularly in AL settings. AI integration mostly occurs in the pre-writing (idea generation) and drafting (feedback/refinement) phases. Students generally perceive AI positively, reporting increased creativity, particularly through image generation, and enhanced motivation and engagement. AI co-creation is linked to improvements in textual quality for less proficient learners, such as better logical structure and grammatical accuracy. This review highlights the potential of AI as a co-creation tool in the creative writing classroom.

TI EIL input, gender, and metacognitive listening strategies in
   CEFR-aligned primary EFL
SO PORTA LINGUARUM
LA English
DT Article
DE Metacognitive strategies; EFL listening comprehension; CEFR; gender
   differences; English as an International Language (EIL)
ID INSTRUCTION
AB This study investigates the use of metacognitive listening strategies among Spanish primary school learners of English as a Foreign Language (EFL) and examines the influence of input variability, gender, and grade level. A quantitative, quasi-experimental cross-sectional design was employed with a sample of 1,038 fifth-and sixth-grade students. Participants were divided into a control group exposed to native English input and an experimental group exposed to English as an International Language (EIL). Data were collected using an adapted Metacognitive Awareness Listening Questionnaire (MALQ) and a tailored Listening Comprehension Test. Results revealed that exposure to native English yielded significantly higher overall listening performance and directed attention compared to EIL. Significant gender differences were observed: female learners demonstrated superior performance in planning-evaluation, directed attention, problem-solving, and overall metacognitive awareness, while males exhibited a higher reliance on mental translation. Furthermore, a developmental paradox was noted: sixth-grade students reported lower explicit metacognitive strategy use despite achieving higher listening scores, suggesting a shift towards cognitive automaticity. These findings highlight the need for sustained, multidimensional, and personalized metacognitive pedagogical interventions in primary EFL contexts.

AB The project "The development of an interlinguistic school grammar: towards reflective language teaching in multilingual contexts" (Egramint), in which this article is included, aims to develop a cross-linguistic school grammar that promotes reflection throughout the language teaching-learning process. TI Towards an integrative approach to teaching Spanish pronunciation to
   Mandarin-speaking learners
SO PORTA LINGUARUM
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE pronunciation; Spanish as an additional language; Mandarin-speaking
   learners; Verbo-Tonal Method; Melodic Analysis of Speech; Task-Based
   Learning
AB This article presents an integrative approach to teaching Spanish pronunciation to Mandarin-speaking learners within a communicative and task-based framework. It combines principles from Melodic Analysis of Speech (MAS), the Verbo-Tonal Method (VTM) and Task-Based Language Teaching (TBLT) to design sequences that connect pronunciation work with communicative goals. The proposal is based on a double criterion: corrective, because it addresses phonetic features that may affect intelligibility, and communicative, because it prioritizes forms relevant to oral interaction. Special emphasis is placed on prosody, multimodal perception and the use of melodic curves obtained with Praat, together with Verbo-Tonal techniques such as body movement, tension and combinatorial phonetics. Finally, the article provides examples of activities for upper-A2 and B1 learners that can be adapted to different Spanish as an additional language contexts.

TI The flipped classroom approach: Enhancing behavioral, cognitive,
   emotional engagement, and language learning in elementary language
   classes
SO PORTA LINGUARUM
LA English
DT Article
ID STUDENT ENGAGEMENT; SCHOOL ENGAGEMENT; ACADEMIC-ACHIEVEMENT; MOTIVATION;
   CONTEXT; TEACHER; ENGLISH
AB This study elucidated how a flipped classroom approach influences EFL students' behavioral, cognitive, and emotional engagement, as well as language learning in elementary private language classes. Forty-eight female students (average age 11) were divided into control and experimental groups (24 each). The experimental group received tasks and video clips via a Telegram channel for home study, followed by in-class games and activities to encourage participation and activate prior knowledge. Students' proficiency was assessed before and after the treatment using Babel test samples based on the Nelson Quick Check Placement Tests. Engagement was measured using the school engagement scale by Fredricks et al. (2005), which assesses behavioral, emotional, and cognitive dimensions. Data were analyzed using SPSS 26. Results revealed that the flipped classroom approach influenced all types of engagement; the highest difference was observed in cognitive engagement, and the lowest in behavioral engagement. Regarding language learning, the results indicated that the flipped approach led to better outcomes in the experimental group. Hence, the findings highlight the effectiveness of the flipped technique in enhancing language learning and positively affecting student engagement in classroom activities. These results could be beneficial for curriculum designers aiming to incorporate more entertaining and operational activities. Keywords: Behavioral engagement, Cognitive engagement, Emotional engagement, Flipped classroom approach, Elementary English language students

TI Exploring how psychological capital and grit shape language learners'
   psychological well-being in AI-based educational contexts: A bifactor
   analysis
SO PORTA LINGUARUM
LA English
DT Article
DE Artificial intelligence-based contexts; Grit; Psychological capital;
   Psychological well-being; Self-Determination theory
ID PERFORMANCE
AB Integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) into language teaching has changed learning settings by increasing access to feedback, practice, and individualized support. However, the psychological mechanisms sustaining students' Psychological Well-being (PWB) remain largely overlooked. Based on Self-Determination Theory (SDT), this research examines how two intrinsic resources, PsyCap and L2 grit, boost PWB in AI-based contexts, as both are vital for protecting PWB in feedback-rich, demanding environments. Thus, A total of 498 Chinese learners of Japanese from four universities who actively use AI-based apps participated. Three validated questionnaires adapted to AI settings were administered online and the data were analyzed using a bifactor modeling approach to disentangle the shared and unique contributions of grit and PsyCap to PWB. Results showed that both PsyCap and grit significantly predicted PWB, with the bifactor model showed that a general psychological resource factor explained a substantial proportion of the variance in PWB, revealing that a general psychological resource factor accounted for substantial variance, while specific dimensions of each provided unique contributions. By integrating positive psychology and SDT in AI-based learning, this research advances theory and suggests practical interventions that promote PsyCap and grit to develop learners' PWB.

TI Unpacking L2 teachers' and learners' reflections on the hidden
   challenges of AI-assisted language education
SO PORTA LINGUARUM
LA English
DT Article
DE Artificial intelligence (AI); AI-assisted language education;
   challenges; L2 classrooms; phenomenological study
AB This phenomenological study investigated the challenges experienced by Iranian and Saudi teachers and learners in artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted L2 classrooms. Using maximum variation sampling, a total of 117 participants were selected from diverse educational institutions in Iran and Saudi Arabia. Drawing on written reflective narratives and semi-structured interviews, the study revealed that AI integration generated a set of educational, emotional, and ethical challenges that transformed language education practices. Educational challenges included misalignment between AI outputs and curricular goals, insufficient institutional training, and learners' overreliance on automated feedback. Emotionally, both teachers and learners reported heightened anxiety, reduced confidence, and frustration arising from conflicting human-AI feedback and rapidly evolving technological demands. Ethically, participants highlighted concerns about academic dishonesty, data privacy risks, cultural insensitivity, and unequal access to reliable AI tools. Taken together, these findings demonstrate that AI is not merely a technological enhancement but a transformative force that reconfigures pedagogical routines, affective experiences, and moral responsibilities. The study concludes by outlining theoretical and practical implications for responsible, context-sensitive, and educationally meaningful AI integration in L2 contexts.

TI Effects of the typological proximity between Portuguese and Spanish on
   the use of derived words in PFL
SO PORTA LINGUARUM
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Bilingual lexicon; foreign language acquisition; morphology; word
   formation
ID RECOGNITION; BILINGUALS; COGNATE; REPRESENTATIONS; ACQUISITION;
   FREQUENCY; OVERLAP
AB In this paper, we present the results of a study on the effects of typological proximity between Portuguese and Spanish on the use of derived words (DW) by learners of Portuguese as a foreign language (PFL) at different stages of their (inter)linguistic development. Based on a comparative study of the lexicogenetic constructions used in a corpus of texts written by PFL learners in immersion and their Spanish counterparts, we assess the extent of the coincidence of word construction patterns and morpholexical constituents (bases and affixes) in the two languages, in order to gauge how this knowledge influences the production of derived words at different levels of proficiency (from A1 to C1). According to the data collected, learners who have Spanish as their L1 accurately instantiate (85.7% on average) the construction patterns of Portuguese, in line with the high degree of coincidence of the patterns and affixes used in these two languages. The deviations, in addition to being insignificant, mainly concern the graphic representation of lexical bases.

TI The Possibilities and Challenges of Generative Artificial Intelligence
   for Initial Teacher Education in Australia
SO AUSTRALIAN JOURNAL OF TEACHER EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
AB This paper examines the impact of Generative AI (GenAI) on pre-service teachers (PSTs) and its future role in Initial Teacher Education (ITE) courses. Drawing from a polychronic and polyphonic research methodology (Jandric et al., 2019; Matusov et al., 2019), the six participants, experienced Initial Teacher Educators, identify the opportunities GenAI offers for enhancing teaching, streamlining administration, and providing personalized learning. They also articulate the challenges GenAI presents: bias, ethical and authenticity issues and copyright. The Teacher Educators agree that PSTs must become technically proficient and critically discerning towards GenAI content, and they highlight the need for personalized and context-specific assessment methods. The participants also see addressing inclusivity and equity as crucial, ensuring GenAI tools are accessible to all students, including those in rural, remote, and First Nations communities in Australia. These reflections are aligned to the 'Australian Framework for Generative Artificial Intelligence in Schools' six principles: Teaching and Learning, Human and Social Wellbeing, Transparency, Fairness, Accountability, and Privacy, Security, and Safety. Drawing on this small, policy-relevant study, they conclude that ITE programs must be dynamic and adapt to the introduction of GenAI tools to prepare PSTs in their future classrooms, ensuring the PSTs can harness the potential of GenAI thoughtfully, ethically, and in ways that benefit themselves and their students.

TI Indicators of Mid-Career Teacher Quality through Perspectives of Key
   Stakeholders
SO AUSTRALIAN JOURNAL OF TEACHER EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
ID STUDENT-ACHIEVEMENT; EDUCATION
AB The ongoing quest of quality education has focused on teaching quality in K-12 classrooms globally, as evidenced by recent research, reviews, and media coverage. Yet, identifying, defining, and measuring 'teacher quality' remains a complex challenge, particularly during the crucial mid-career stage. The focus on mid-career teachers in educational research is often neglected, when compared with early career teachers or teachers in leadership. This qualitative study explores the characteristics that mid-career teachers, teacher leaders and accreditation personnel perceive as the indicators of a quality mid-career teacher. Drawing on semi-structured interviews with 29 participants including 23 mid-career teachers, five school principals, and a regulatory authority representative in Australia, the United Arab Emirates, and Pakistan, the research sheds light on factors that contribute to mid-career teacher quality. Thematic analysis revealed 794 indicators, 45 sub-themes, and eight themes of mid-career teacher quality. The participants' perceptions revealed 'knowledge of teaching practice' as the most frequently discussed element. Next in terms of frequency was 'content knowledge', followed by 'collaboration and relationship building'. This research lays the groundwork for future action focusing on locating valid and reliable measures of the identified indicators. This, in turn, will empower future efforts to promote and improve mid-career teacher quality.

TI Investigating the Changes in Attitudes Towards Science Among Pre-Service
   Elementary Teachers Enrolled in A Science Methods Course Using a New
   Version of the Test of Science Related Attitudes
SO AUSTRALIAN JOURNAL OF TEACHER EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE learning environment; science methods; pre-service teachers;
   constructivist approach; attitudes towards science
ID STUDENTS ATTITUDES; SELF-EFFICACY; EDUCATION; ENVIRONMENTS; BELIEFS;
   TAIWAN
AB This article examines the changes in student attitudes towards science among pre-service elementary teachers (PSETs), who were enrolled in a science methods course at a large public university in Texas, USA. A new version of the Test of Science Related Attitudes (TOSRA) called TOSRA-3 was used to measure six dimensions of attitudes towards science. TOSRA-3 was created in an effort to create a more economical, 35 items versus 70 items, version of the original TOSRA. TOSRA-3 was found to be valid and reliable for use with PSETs. Factor analysis suggests a six scale structure with a Cronbach's Alpha for each scale ranged from 0.67 to 0.91. Independent sample t-tests and Hedge's g showed significant gains in three of the six TOSRA-3 scales, namely, Normality of Scientists, Attitudes to Scientific Inquiry, and Leisure and Career Interest in Science. Overall, the study supports that science methods instruction that focuses on constructivist learning theory, hands-on and minds-on learning and the 5E instructional model has a positive effect on the PSETs' attitudes towards science.

LA English
DT Article
DE intellectual virtues; lifelong learning; higher education; pedagogy;
   learner dispositions
AB Higher education aims to develop graduates with specific professional and disciplinary expertise and lifelong learning capabilities. We argue that instruction for these learning dispositions, conceptualised in this study as intellectual virtues, is challenging and complex. AB In this paper I discuss the perceived tensions in navigating an Explicit Instruction approach with a Culturally Responsive Pedagogy at the cultural interface. TI Undercooked or Over Easy? Perceptions of Initial Teacher Educators on
   the Growth of Alternative Authority to Teach Contracts
SO AUSTRALIAN JOURNAL OF TEACHER EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Key Words-Pre-service teachers; teacher shortage; Phenomenological
   study; ITE providers; AAT pathways
ID ATTRITION
AB The practice of employing pre-service teachers (PST) in schools prior to the completion of their teacher training, has grown over the last three years as the teacher shortage across Australia and the world worsens. This study examines the perceived impact of Alternative Authority to Teach (AAT) contracts on the teaching profession through the lens of university lecturers working within the Initial Teacher Education (ITE) space. This phenomenological research sought to gain a wider understanding of the impact ofAAT contracts on ITE stakeholders and their PST. Qualitative semi-structured interviews were conducted with eleven university lecturers. A thematic analysis of the discourse arising from these interviews was conducted and found two distinct areas of concern, those relating to the student and employer, and PST and the university. University lecturers unanimously felt their voices were not heard, since they were not given a seat at the negotiation table between schools and registering bodies, prior to PSTs undertaking a teaching contract. These findings demonstrate the need for strategies that engender greater awareness of and support for PST working in the school system while studying. The combined voices of Initial Teacher Educators call for all stakeholders to be actively involved in the implementation of a holistic, purposeful and accountable approach to addressing the teacher shortage in sustainable, future focused endeavours.

TI Assessment instruments for e-professionalism in healthcare: a systematic
   review
SO BMC MEDICAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE E-professionalism; Social media; Nursing; Pharmacy; Medicine; Dentistry
ID SOCIAL MEDIA; ONLINE PROFESSIONALISM; STUDENTS; PERCEPTIONS; PHARMACY;
   COSMIN; PERSPECTIVES; ATTITUDES
AB Introduction E-professionalism represents the foundation guiding the conduct of health professionals on social media. Assessing e-professionalism allows the identification of gaps in professional education and supports institutions in adapting to technological changes. Gathering evidence on the quality of available instruments may promote reliable and consistent measurement of this construct.Objective To evaluate the evidence of validity of instruments used to assess e-professionalism among students and healthcare professionals.Methods A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the systematic review manual of the Consensus-based Standards for the Selection of Health Measurement Instruments (COSMIN). The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (ID CRD42023454825). The search was carried out in July 2025 in the PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science, ERIC, and Scopus databases. Articles reporting e-professionalism instruments with evidence of validity were included, targeting professionals and/or students in Nursing, Pharmacy, Medicine, and Dentistry, with no restrictions regarding language or year of publication. The quality of the instruments was analyzed using COSMIN criteria.Results The search identified 4,616 studies, with 28 included, published between 2009 and 2025. The instruments were predominantly directed toward students (n = 20; 71.4%). Overall, the instruments contained an average of 26 items and three subscales. Only one of the studies established cutoff points for interpreting the results. Regarding psychometric properties, only four of the nine recommended by COSMIN were investigated, with emphasis on content validity (n = 24; 85.7%), internal consistency (n = 8; 28.5%), and structural validity (n = 7; 25%).Conclusions This review highlights the need for greater conceptual consensus regarding e-professionalism and its domains, as well as the development of instruments with robust validity for both students and health professionals. The lack of reliable tools limits comparisons and evaluations, reinforcing the importance of research that integrates theoretical definition with psychometric validation to accurately reflect the construct.

DT Article
DE Health literacy; Health literacy competency; Medical humanities; Medical
   education; Curriculum development; Medical student clerkship
ID COMMUNICATION; PROFESSIONALS
AB Background Low health literacy is linked to poorer quality of life and health outcomes. However, one-third of healthcare professionals lacked awareness or understanding. This highlights the importance of incorporating health literacy into the education of healthcare professionals. Our study aimed to integrate health literacy into medical clerkship curricula and evaluate the effectiveness of educational programs.Methods We recruited fifth-year medical students in the family medicine clerkship from October 2023 to January 2026. The health literacy education program included lectures, simulated case-based videos in the classroom, and observation and hands-on practice in a real-world clinic. In the multiple-choice questions within the Concept and Evaluation Dimension, the average score improved from 4.11 to 5.30 points, reflecting a 29.02% increase. TI Perceived stress, stress-related symptoms, and support-based coping in
   healthcare students: insights from a cross-sectional study in the United
   Arab Emirates
SO BMC MEDICAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Perceived stress; Coping mechanisms; Medical students; Academic
   performance; Mental well-being; Burnout; Psychological distress
ID UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS; ACADEMIC STRESS; STRATEGIES; COVID-19
AB Background Healthcare students experience significant stress due to rigorous academic demands, frequent assessments, and clinical responsibilities. Prolonged stress can negatively impact academic performance, cognitive abilities, and mental well-being. Understanding stress levels and coping mechanisms among healthcare students is essential for developing targeted interventions to enhance their well-being and academic success. This study aims to assess the prevalence of stress and explore the coping strategies employed by healthcare students. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among healthcare students at a medical university in Ajman, UAE. A self-administered questionnaire was used to collect sociodemographic data, stress levels using the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10), and coping mechanisms. The final sample consisted of 938 students, recruited using convenience sampling. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the data, and chi-square tests were performed to assess associations between stress levels and sociodemographic variables. Data analysis was conducted using IBM (R) SPSS Statistics version 29.0. Results Among the participants, 71.1% experienced moderate stress, while 13.8% reported high stress. Stress levels were significantly associated with college affiliation (p = 0.009) and nationality (p = 0.044). The most commonly reported stress-related manifestations were difficulty sleeping (44.5%), feeling overwhelmed (44.1%), and appetite loss (42.5%). Coping strategies varied, with 42.9% of students sometimes relying on parental guidance, 40.5% seeking support from mentors, and 43% turning to friends for stress relief. A significant association was found between coping mechanisms and perceived stress levels (p < 0.001), indicating that students who frequently sought social support experienced lower stress levels. Conclusions The study highlights the high prevalence of stress among healthcare students and emphasizes the critical role of social support in stress management. Institutional interventions, such as mentorship programs and stress management workshops, could be effective in reducing stress and improving student well-being. Future research should explore the long-term effectiveness of different coping mechanisms and the impact of structured academic interventions on stress reduction.

TI Development and validation of the Scholarship of Teaching and Learning
   Assessment Questionnaire (SoTLAQ) among health professions educators
SO BMC MEDICAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Scholarship; Teaching; Teacher; Medical education; Questionnaire
ID GUIDE; MOTIVATION
AB Background With the increasing recognition of the role of the scholarship of teaching and learning in enhancing educational quality and fostering the professional growth of health professions educators, the availability of a rigorously validated instrument to measure their awareness, attitudes, and experiences has become essential. This study aimed to design and validate a questionnaire to assess the awareness, attitudes, and experiences of faculty members involved in health professions education regarding their involvement in scholarship of teaching and learning activities.Methods This exploratory mixed-methods research was conducted in accordance with the AMEE Guide No. 87 framework, a structured approach for instrument development and validation, to develop and validate the Scholarship of Teaching Assessment Questionnaire (SOTLAQ). Participants were recruited from faculty members at Tehran University of Medical Sciences (TUMS), Iran, using purposive sampling for the qualitative phase and convenience sampling for the quantitative phase. The initial item pool was generated from a literature review, semi-structured interviews, and a focus group discussion. The extracted codes were assessed through expert panel deliberations involving six experts in the scholarship of teaching. Eight experts assessed content validity, while face validity was evaluated through cognitive interviews with five faculty members to ensure item clarity and transparency. Construct validity was examined using exploratory factor analysis, and reliability was determined by calculating Cronbach's alpha based on responses from 165 faculty members.Results From the semi-structured interviews (176 codes), the literature review (37 codes), and the focus group (21 codes), a total of 30 merged codes were initially identified. Following the expert panel review, a 24-item questionnaire was finalized. The content validity index (CVI) and content validity ratio (CVR) exceeded 0.75. Exploratory factor analysis identified five factors, including "perceived awareness," "perceived skills," "perceived motivation and support," "perceived enablers and drivers," and "perceived barriers and challenges," which explained 63.3% of the variance. The overall Cronbach's alpha was 0.906.Conclusion The SoTLAQ questionnaire is a valid and reliable tool for assessing key dimensions that affect faculty engagement in the scholarship of teaching activities. This questionnaire may be useful in planning educational interventions, empowerment programs, and policymaking in the field of medical education. However, further validation in diverse institutional settings and different countries is recommended before its widespread use.

TI The Anatomage table in medical education: perceptions and associated
   factors among students in Rwanda
SO BMC MEDICAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Anatomy; Anatomage Table; Virtual dissection; Perceived benefits
ID CADAVERIC DISSECTION
AB Background Gross anatomy is foundational in medical education and is traditionally taught through cadaveric dissection. However, post-COVID-19 technological advancements have introduced digital tools, such as the anatomage table (AT), which offers interactive 3D virtual dissection to enhance learning outcomes and overcome logistical challenges. Objective This study assessed the perceived educational benefits of AT and associated factors among medical students at the University of Global Health Equity (UGHE), Rwanda. Methods A cross-sectional analytical study using a structured, validated questionnaire was conducted among 148 first- to third-year Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery students. Data were collected using the KoboToolbox and analyzed using SPSS. Chi-square tests and logistic regression were used to identify factors associated with perceived educational benefits of AT. A p-value < 0.05 with a 95% confidence interval was considered statistically significant. Results Of the 135 participating medical students (response rate of 91.2%), 83.0% perceived AT as beneficial, while 83.7% demonstrated good practice and a favorable attitude toward its use. Additionally, 65.9% of the participants reported improved learning due to the use of AT. Logistic regression identified female sex (AOR = 3.51, CI: 1.26-9.76), good practice (AOR = 3.05, CI: 1.26-7.36), and perceived learning improvement (AOR = 4.45, CI: 2.26-9.13) as significant predictors of perceived benefits. Conclusion This study shows that students perceived AT as a beneficial educational tool for learning gross anatomy and associated it with a positive attitude and improved learning experience.

TI Assessment of pain neurophysiology knowledge among healthcare students
   in Bayero University Kano, Nigeria: a cross-sectional study
SO BMC MEDICAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Pain Neuroscience Education; Pain Neurophysiology Knowledge; Healthcare
   Education; Knowledge Assessment; Bayero University Kano; Nigeria;
   Africa; Chronic Pain
ID REVISED NEUROPHYSIOLOGY; NEUROSCIENCE EDUCATION; QUESTIONNAIRE
AB Background Pain Neurophysiology Knowledge (PNK) refers to the understanding of the biological and physiological mechanisms underlying the experience of pain. For healthcare students, a solid grasp of pain neurophysiology is essential for the effective future management of patients experiencing pain, particularly chronic pain. The aim of this study was to assess the level of PNK among healthcare undergraduate students studying Dentistry, Medicine, Nursing, Optometry, and Physiotherapy at Bayero University Kano (BUK), Nigeria. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted using the Revised Neurophysiology of Pain Questionnaire (RNPQ) to evaluate PNK among healthcare students at BUK. Whole population sampling was employed to recruit registered healthcare students across the various disciplines at BUK. Descriptive statistics (frequencies, percentages, and means) were used to characterize the sample. Differences in scores between the study disciplines and levels of study were analyzed using one-way ANOVA and independent t-tests (IBM SPSS version 23). One-way ANOVA was used to compare mean scores across multiple disciplines and clinical levels where more than two groups were present. Where comparisons involved only two groups, independent samples t-tests were applied. Significance level was set at p < 0.05. Results A total of 500 students from the Physiotherapy, Nursing, Medicine, Dentistry, and Optometry programs participated. The majority of participants (66.2%) were aged 21-25 years, and 57.2% were male. Medical students represented the largest group (27.0%), and second-year clinical students across disciplines comprised 38% of the sample. The mean PNK score across participants from all disciplines was 6.31, indicating moderate knowledge. Statistically significant differences in PNK across clinical years were observed within the Medicine and Nursing programs (p < 0.05). Conclusion / implications Healthcare students at BUK demonstrated average knowledge of pain neurophysiology. This finding suggests a gap in PNK within the study population, which warrants further investigation to better understand the underlying factors contributing to the moderate knowledge levels observed. Future research should explore potential influences such as curricular content, teaching strategies, clinical exposure, and interprofessional education experiences, as well as institutional and contextual factors that may shape students' understanding of pain neurophysiology.

TI Learning to engage in clinical research: a qualitative study developing
   a behavioural pathway model among nurses in China
SO BMC MEDICAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Research engagement; Research literacy; Clinical nurses; Health
   professions education; Qualitative research; COM-B model
AB Background Developing the capacity of health professionals to engage in research and practice improvement is an important goal of health professions education. In nursing, research literacy is considered a key capability that enables clinicians to understand research, formulate practice-based questions, and initiate research or quality improvement activities. In China, rapid expansion of nursing education has strengthened academic preparation; however, the ability of clinical nurses to translate clinical problems into research or improvement initiatives remains uneven across practice settings. Little is known about how nurses develop research literacy in clinical environments and how workplace conditions shape their engagement in research-related practice.Methods This qualitative study used semi-structured interviews with 20 clinical nurses from multiple departments in a tertiary teaching hospital in China. Participants were purposively sampled to capture variation in career stage, educational background, and research exposure. Interviews explored how nurses understood research, interacted around research ideas, evaluated research value, and attempted to initiate or sustain research or improvement projects. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis, informed by sensitising concepts from research literacy theory and the Capability-Opportunity-Motivation-Behaviour (COM-B) behavioural framework.Results Four interrelated themes were identified. Nurses commonly accessed research evidence but often relied on conclusion-oriented interpretation rather than methodological appraisal, which limited their ability to adapt evidence to local practice. Research-related dialogue was mediated by hierarchy, professional positioning, team climate, and perceived psychological safety. Participants distinguished clinically meaningful research from "formalistic" projects perceived as procedural, symbolic, or driven mainly by institutional requirements. This distinction suggested that nurses were not rejecting research itself, but were critically judging whether research activity was clinically meaningful, morally legitimate, and feasible within everyday practice.Translating clinical concerns into research or improvement activities emerged as a fragile and non-linear pathway: ideas could be initiated, stalled, faded, or reactivated depending on workload pressures, leadership support, organisational opportunity, psychological safety, and perceived clinical meaning.Conclusions Engaging in research in clinical nursing appears to be a socially situated professional practice rather than an individual technical skill. Research engagement develops through the interaction of research literacy, professional positioning, psychological safety, motivational commitment, and organisational opportunity within clinical workplaces. Based on these findings, the study proposes a heuristic behavioural pathway model describing how nurses move from interpreting research and recognising clinical problems to evaluating research value and attempting research or improvement action. The model highlights that this process is recursive and contingent rather than a stable linear progression, and may help identify where research engagement is likely to be interrupted or sustained in clinical nursing practice.

TI Integrating problem-based learning with virtual simulation in trauma
   orthopedic education: effects on learning outcomes and student
   satisfaction
SO BMC MEDICAL EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Trauma orthopedics; Problem-based learning; Virtual simulation; Medical
   education; Clinical skills; Critical thinking
ID FRACTURE; REALITY; UTILITY; MODELS
AB Background Trauma orthopedics is a key component of orthopedic clinical education, but its teaching is often limited by complex fracture patterns, high demands for spatial understanding, and insufficient opportunities for hands-on practice. Although problem-based learning (PBL) and virtual simulation have each shown educational value, evidence regarding their combined use in trauma orthopedic teaching remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of an integrated PBL and virtual simulation teaching model in trauma orthopedic education. Methods This assessor-blinded randomized controlled study included 50 clinical medical students undertaking internships at the First Affiliated Hospital of Wannan Medical University between July 2024 and June 2025. Participants were randomly assigned to a control group (n = 25), which received traditional lecture-based teaching, or an experimental group (n = 25), which received PBL combined with virtual simulation. Outcomes included theoretical knowledge, clinical skills, critical thinking ability, student evaluation of teaching effectiveness, and teaching satisfaction. Data were analyzed using t tests and chi-square tests. Results No significant between-group differences were observed in baseline theoretical knowledge or clinical skills scores before teaching. After the intervention, the experimental group achieved significantly higher written examination scores than the control group (88.48 +/- 4.02 vs. 77.04 +/- 5.31,mean difference = 11.44,95% CI: 8.76 - 14.12, p < 0.01) and significantly higher practical operation scores (86.28 +/- 3.18 vs. 76.52 +/- 3.39,mean difference = 9.76,95% CI :7.89 - 11.63,p < 0.01). The experimental group also showed higher total critical thinking scores (314.12 +/- 10.68 vs. 270.28 +/- 19.76,mean difference = 43.84,95% CI: 34.70 - 52.98, p < 0.05), overall teaching effectiveness scores (17.72 +/- 1.24 vs. 12.72 +/- 1.02,mean difference = 5.00,95% CI: 4.35 to 5.65,p < 0.01), and total teaching satisfaction scores (86.96 +/- 6.46 vs. 70.24 +/- 8.71,mean difference = 16.72,95% CI:12.35 - 21.09,p < 0.05). Conclusions The integration of PBL with virtual simulation improved theoretical performance, clinical skills, critical thinking, and learning satisfaction in trauma orthopedic teaching, and may represent an effective strategy for clinical education reform in this field.

TI The Role of Critical Thinking and Social Cure Approach in Collaborative
   Physics Learning Based on Project-Based Learning to Enhance Student
   Well-Being
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL CULTURAL AND PSYCHOLOGICAL STUDIES
LA English
DT Article
DE critical thinking; physics education; project-based learning; social
   cure approach; student well-being
ID PSYCHOLOGICAL SENSE; MEMBERSHIP; SCALE
AB This study examines the roles of critical thinking and the social cure approach in collaborative physics learning environments grounded in Project-Based Learning (PBL) and their impact on student well-being. Adopting a concurrent embedded QUAL+quan mixed-methods design, data were collected from 40 undergraduate physics students at Universitas Islam Negeri Raden Intan Lampung through surveys, focus groups, interviews, creative reflections, and ethnographic field notes across an 8-week intervention. Repeated measures ANOVA indicated large-effect improvements in critical thinking (CTDS; d = 1.0), sense of belonging (PSSM; d = 0.9), well-being (WEMWBS; d = 1.1), and self-efficacy (GSE-6; d = 0.9). Qualitative themes ofenhanced analytical skills, peer-supported belonging, and improved emotional confidence corroborated these patterns. Findings advocate for curricular reforms prioritizing critical thinking and social support within STEM PBL contexts to holistically enhance student well-being.

TI Generative AI and Teacher Education: Evidence from the PRAXIS Framework
   in Italian Educational Contexts
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL CULTURAL AND PSYCHOLOGICAL STUDIES
LA English
DT Article
DE AI literacy; educational contexts; generative AI; professional
   development; teacher education
ID TECHNOLOGY; ACCEPTANCE
AB This article reports findings from a cross-sectional survey of 662 participants in Italian educational contexts, including secondary school students, university students, pre-service teachers, and in-service teachers. Using the PRAXIS framework, which organises GenAI adoption across six dimensions, usage patterns, perceived competence, adequacy of training, expectations of change, interpersonal and institutional trust, and scepticism, the study examines differences in uses, beliefs, and concerns across educational groups. Results show a marked generational divide in adoption, a consistent gap between practical and theoretical competence, and training perceived as inadequate across groups. A pattern of defensive distancing also emerges: teachers recognise that GenAI is changing education, but perceive a smaller impact on their own teaching. Overall, GenAI adoption appears to be advancing faster than the institutional development of critical and pedagogically grounded competences. The study provides an empirical basis for rethinking teacher education as a matter not only of digital upskilling, but also of educational responsibility and learning rights in the transition to GenAI.

   professional lives

AB Increasingly, teachers face demands and pressure to embrace online learning. This study sought out to investigate the complex interplay between teachers' personal and professional lives in home-based online instruction, considering their sex, age, marital status, and type of school variables. TI Bridging the Gap: Student Accessibility, Willingness, and Preferences
   for Telemental Health Services in the School Setting
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL CULTURAL AND PSYCHOLOGICAL STUDIES
LA English
DT Article
DE college students; help-seeking behavior; mixed-methods research;
   Philippines; telemental health
ID HELP
AB Although telemental health (TMH) services offer a promising solution to address students' mental health needs, their adoption in school settings remains limited, particularly in low-resource contexts. This study examined student accessibility, willingness, and preferences for TMH services in the school setting and identified key predictors influencing engagement. A concurrent convergent mixed-methods design was used, combining a survey of 717 college students with focus groups involving students and counselors from two private schools in Nueva Vizcaya, Philippines. Quantitative data were analyzed using multiple linear regression and binary logistic regression, while qualitative data were examined through thematic analysis. TMH was perceived as moderately accessible (M = 3.09) and underutilized, with only 14.8% of students reporting prior use, despite 66% expressing willingness. Accessibility was significantly influenced by communication medium, device ownership, and institutional trust (R-2 = .247, p < .05). Willingness was predicted by perceived helpfulness of school mental health services (OR = 2.59, p < .001), free cost (OR = 4.93, p < .001), comfort discussing mental health with family (OR = 2.71, p = .031), family support (OR = 2.01, p = .035), and prior positive experience with mental health services (OR = 3.09, p = .029). Preferences were most strongly associated with confidentiality and privacy (M = 3.61), and the preference model explained 14.8% of the variance (R-2 = .148). Qualitative findings supported these results while highlighting concerns related to rapport, personalization, and privacy. Students show high willingness to use TMH when barriers related to cost, trust, and privacy are addressed. Hybrid delivery models, family engagement, and institutionally endorsed, culturally responsive implementation may enhance the uptake of TMH services in school-based mental health systems.

TI Comprehensive Analysis of a Multiple-Choice Algebra Assessment
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL CULTURAL AND PSYCHOLOGICAL STUDIES
LA English
DT Article
DE college and advanced algebra; item analysis; teacher education; test
   de-velopment; validity and reliability
ID VALIDITY; RELIABILITY
AB This study developed and validated a 70-item multiple-choice College and Advanced Algebra (Math 101) midterm test designed to diagnose least-mastered competencies. Development followed a three-phase process: (1) preparation, involving syllabus mapping and a Table of Specifications (TOS) to ensure balanced content coverage and guide item writing; (2) development, which included expert review of content and technical quality and a tryout administration; and (3) implementation, featuring uniform test administration procedures, scoring verification, item analysis, and reliability estimation. Item analysis resulted in 48 retained items, 20 for revision, and 2 rejected, supporting continued refinement and item-bank development.

TI Extending the Validation of the 3SQ to Higher Education: Factor
   Structure and Reliability in a Large Italian University Sample
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL CULTURAL AND PSYCHOLOGICAL STUDIES
LA English
DT Article
DE confirmatory factor analysis; higher education; instrument validation;
   reliability; soft skills
ID MEASUREMENT INVARIANCE; ALPHA
AB This Research Note reports a psychometric population-extension validation of the Soft Skills Self-evaluation Questionnaire (3SQ) in higher education. Data were collected through the completion ofan online digital form in 2024-2025 from university students enrolled at three Italian universities (N = 2,130). Age was computed from year of birth and survey year, yielding valid values for n = 2,116 (M = 23.21, SD = 4.38; Mdn = 23, IQR = 21-24). We tested the established 10-factor structure via confirmatory factor analysis (maximum likelihood). Model fit was acceptable to good, chi 2(734) = 4246.98, p < .001; CFI = .920; TLI = .911; RMSEA = .047. Standardized loadings were consistently positive and substantively meaningful across all dimensions. Internal consistency was satisfactory to excellent across scales (alpha and omega range = .79-.93), with excellent reliability for the total score (alpha = .923; omega = .922). Overall, findings support the structural validity and reliability of the 3SQ when administered to university students, extending prior evidence from school-based samples and supporting its use for research and formativepurposes in higher education.

TI EXPLORING THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN MENTAL HEALTH AND METACOGNITION AMONG
   MEDICAL STUDENTS: IMPLICATIONS FOR EDUCATIONAL PRACTICE
SO ZBORNIK INSTITUTA ZA PEDAGOSKA ISTRAZIVANJA
LA English
DT Article
DE metacognitive learning strategies; institutional prevention programs;
   youth mental health
ID PERCEIVED SELF-EFFICACY; DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS; YOUNG-PEOPLE; RELIABILITY;
   PREVALENCE; VALIDITY
AB According to leading theories of successful learning, students are active participants in the process and regulate their learning, meaning they take responsibility and manage this process. The aim of this study is to assess learning approaches and the use of metacognitive strategies and their significance in relation to the mental health of students training to become healthcare professionals. The State Metacognitive Inventory (SMI) was used to assess students' metacognitive processes, and the Mental Health Inventory (MHI) to evaluate their mental health. The study included 363 medical students from Novi Sad, comprising 34 males and 329 females, aged 18 to 29 years. Among the students, moderate levels of anxiety and depressive symptoms were observed, with mean scores indicating a mid-range level on the scales. Reported symptoms included feelings of nervousness, worry, tension, sadness, and worthlessness, while students simultaneously demonstrated relatively high behavioural control. Metacognitive strategies exhibited only weak loadings on mental health indicators, suggesting that moderate levels of strategy use were weakly related to psychological symptoms. This association may be viewed as an indication rather than a causal effect, given the study design. These findings point to the potential importance of further strengthening metacognitive awareness and regulatory strategies. The results emphasize the importance of systematically integrating metacognitive training into higher education and developing structured programs that enhance both academic competencies and students' mental health. Institutional support and preventive interventions are crucial for reducing psychological distress and improving overall mental well-being among students. These findings further underscore that fostering metacognitive skills may serve as a supportive resource in coping with stress and emotional challenges in demanding academic environments and highlight the necessity of embedding such strategies in educational practice.

TI DOES INSTRUCTIONAL CLARITY MODERATE THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN
   SOCIOECONOMIC STATUS AND STUDENT ACHIEVEMENT? A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS
   BASED ON THE TIMSS 2023 DATA
SO ZBORNIK INSTITUTA ZA PEDAGOSKA ISTRAZIVANJA
LA English
DT Article
DE socioeconomic status; educational inequalities; instructional clarity;
   student achievement
ID ACADEMIC-ACHIEVEMENT
AB Reducing the effect of social status on learning outcomes constitutes one of the crucial challenges for contemporary education systems. This study sought to determine whether instructional clarity, as a teaching quality dimension, could moderate the effect of socioeconomic status (SES) on student achievement. The analysis was based on TIMSS 2023 data collected in 29 European education systems. The study examined a simple moderation model, with instructional clarity moderating the relationship between SES and achievement in mathematics and science tests. The results showed that the strength of the SES-achievement correlation varied across education systems, mostly proving moderate. Instructional clarity showed the potential to moderate the SES-achievement relationship, although in different ways across different education systems. In the ones with less pronounced educational inequalities, greater clarity weakened the SES achievement correlation, with students from the lowest SES backgrounds benefiting most from high instructional clarity. Conversely, in systems with more pronounced inequalities, instructional clarity proved able to even strengthen the SES-achievement correlation in the case of mathematics. The compensatory potential of high-quality instruction is shaped by the wider educational and social contexts. This has significant implications for inequality-reducing education policy measures.

TI SUCCESS IN GRADUATE EDUCATION FROM STUDENTS' PERSPECTIVES: A
   PHENOMENOLOGICAL STUDY*
SO ZBORNIK INSTITUTA ZA PEDAGOSKA ISTRAZIVANJA
LA English
DT Article
DE academic success; educational sciences; graduate students; phenomenology
AB This study explores how graduate students in educational sciences define academic success and the factors influencing it. Using a phenomenological approach in methodology, thirteen master's and PhD students voluntarily participated. The analysis followed the stages of Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA), moving from detailed initial noting to the development of emergent themes and cross-case interpretations. The data analysis revealed four themes in students' success definitions. These are academic development, personal or intrinsic values, professional development, and social or cultural values. Academia-oriented students emphasized publishing, academic identity, and specialization, while profession-oriented students highlighted practical application, personal growth, and social recognition. Factors shaping their success were grouped as personal, family, cultural, supervision, peer, field, profession, and faculty related. Supervisor support, peer collaboration, and academic flexibility served as key enablers. However, time constraints, institutional barriers, gender roles, and limited workplace incentives appeared as common challenges. Overall, the findings indicate that success in graduate education cannot be understood only as an outcome of individual effort. Rather, it emerges through the interplay between personal aspirations and the conditions. These results point to the importance of more flexible, supportive, and socially responsive graduate programs in education.

TI PREVENTION OF CYBERBULLYING IN SCHOOLS-STUDENTS' PERSPECTIVE
SO ZBORNIK INSTITUTA ZA PEDAGOSKA ISTRAZIVANJA
LA English
DT Article
DE cyberbullying; prevention; preventive role of schools; STUDENTS'
   PERSPECTIVE
ID DIGITAL-AGE; INTERVENTIONS; PROGRAMS
AB Cyberbullying is becoming a more frequent and serious problem among students, thus indicating the importance of its prevention. The school context is recognised as a significant and suitable area for preventive action; therefore, research on students' perspectives on cyberbullying can substantially contribute to understanding the role of schools in its prevention. The focus of this research is to explore the students' perceptions of the presence and effectiveness of preventive measures in schools. The research included 856 students from the 5th to the 8th grade of elementary schools in Belgrade. Using descriptive statistics, it was established that only half of the students recognise the preventive efforts of schools, and that only a third of them are informed about the activities of the team for the protection of students against violence. The factor analysis identified three dimensions of students' perceptions of preventive measures effectiveness: educational, controlling and supportive. The findings indicated that students attribute the greatest preventive potential to the appropriate support to students and positive school climate, whereas they perceive the restrictions as less effective. The conclusion emphasises that it is essential to transform the existing preventive practice, which is not sufficiently oriented toward the holistic model and integration of socio-emotional learning, digital empowerment, and authentic involvement of all participants in creating a stimulative and safe school environment.
