TI Knowledge sharing: The key to improving medical error reporting in
   nursing
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Knowledge management; knowledge sharing; medical error; nursing staff;
   patient safety
ID MANAGEMENT
AB BACKGROUND: Medical errors pose significant clinical, economic, and safety challenges in healthcare. Error reporting enhances learning and reduces incidents, yet barriers persist. This study evaluates the impact of knowledge management on reducing barriers to the medical error reporting among nurses. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A quasi-experimental study was conducted in 2024 at Velayat Hospital, Damghan, Iran, with 62 nurses (bachelor's/master's degree holders) randomly assigned to the intervention (n = 31) and control (n = 31) groups. The intervention group used an anonymous reporting bot, received "lessons learned" feedback every 10 days, and participated in the brainstorming sessions over 3 months. The control group followed standard reporting without feedback. Barriers were assessed pre- and post-intervention using Mardani's Medical Error Reporting Barriers Questionnaire. Data were analyzed with SPSS v22 using paired and independent t-tests. RESULTS: In both the control and intervention groups, women represented 83.9% in the control group and 65.5% in the intervention group. Those holding a bachelor's degree accounted for 90.3% in the control group and 96.6% in the intervention group, and permeant employment 61.3% in the control group and 65.5% in the intervention group. Women comprised 83.9% (control) and 65.5% (intervention) of participants. The intervention group showed the significant reduction in barriers (mean: 3.36 +/- 0.68 to 2.53 +/- 0.40, P < 0.001), while the control group showed no change (3.26 +/- 0.65 to 3.33 +/- 0.66, P > 0.05). CONCLUSION: Knowledge management significantly reduces barriers to error reporting, offering a scalable strategy for health policy to the enhance patient safety.

TI Effectiveness of a breastfeeding education package on breastfeeding
   knowledge, attitude, self-efficacy, and breastfeeding practices among
   women with gestational diabetes mellitus: A randomized controlled trial
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Breastfeeding; education; gestational diabetes mellitus; postpartum
ID INTERVENTION; DURATION; MOTHERS
AB BACKGROUND: Women with Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) frequently encounter challenges that impede successful breastfeeding, despite its significant benefits for postnatal glycemic control. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of the Breastfeeding Education Package (BFEP) on the knowledge, attitude, self-efficacy, and breastfeeding practices among pregnant women with GDM. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This Randomized Controlled Trial was conducted in Selangor, Malaysia, randomized 58 pregnant women with GDM into an Intensive Breastfeeding Intervention (IBI) group (n = 29) or a control group (CG) (n = 29). The IBI group received three individualized dietitian-led education sessions. Knowledge, attitude, and self-efficacy were assessed at baseline and 37 weeks' gestation; breastfeeding practices were monitored for six months post-delivery. RESULTS: A two-way repeated measures ANOVA confirmed the effectiveness of the intervention, revealing a significant difference between the IBI group and the CG in improving breastfeeding knowledge, attitude, and self-efficacy (P < 0.005). The IBI group attained significantly higher mean scores for knowledge (35.76 +/- 5.77), attitude (89.91 +/- 9.9), and self-efficacy (56.02 +/- 8.17) compared to the CG (P < 0.001). This was reflected in practice, as the mean duration of exclusive breastfeeding (EBF) was longer in the IBI group (92.41 +/- 82.14 days) than in the CG (55.59 +/- 74.90 days). Furthermore, a Pearson's correlation within the IBI group identified a small, positive relationship between knowledge and attitude scores and the subsequent length of EBF. CONCLUSION: BFEP is an effective intervention that significantly improves the antenatal knowledge, attitude, and self-efficacy of mothers with GDM. These psychosocial enhancements, in turn, translate into a longer duration of breastfeeding post-delivery.

TI Investigating the relationship between e-health literacy and the
   tendencies and preferences of patients with type 2 diabetes in using
   self-management technologies
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE E-health literacy; self-management; telemedicine; type 2 diabetes
   mellitus
AB BACKGROUND:Type 2 diabetes is known as the most common type of diabetes and requires continuous and comprehensive patient management and support. Diabetes self-management is a set of defined activities and behaviors the patient performs to achieve control and management of diabetes in their daily life. This study examines the relationship between e-health literacy and the tendencies plus preferences of patients with type 2 diabetes in using self-management technologies of their disease in Ferdows city in 2022.MATERIALS AND METHODS:In this descriptive-analytical study, the research population consisted of all clients of health centers and hospitals of Ferdows city, whereby 305 patients with type 2 diabetes were randomly selected and examined. The inclusion criteria were age over 18 years, reading and writing literacy, and being able to use a mobile phone. The collection tool was a three-part questionnaire including a checklist of individual characteristics, a standard 8-question Norman electronic health literacy questionnaire, and a researcher-made questionnaire on the preferences and tendencies of diabetic patients in the field of using mobile health in self-management of the disease. The data were described using descriptive statistics analysis including frequency tables, mean, variance, and standard deviation by SPSS software version 26, after which nonparametric tests such as Mann-Whitney, Kruskal-Wallis, and Spearman's correlation coefficient were used.RESULTS:A total of 305 people participated in this study, of whom 153 (50.2%) were men and the rest were women. The average age of the participants in the research was 50.17 +/- 12.91 years. The average health literacy score of the participants in the study was 27.02 +/- 5.21. The number of people who used methods based on companion health to manage their disease was 278 people; among the various methods, telephone call-based ones were the most frequent with 69.2%, followed by the use of SMS among patients with a relative frequency of 51.5% as the most used method. Out of 305 patients participating, 111 people had not used any of the health-related methods in managing their disease. Most of the people (55.9%) mentioned that they did not know that these methods exist for managing their disease.CONCLUSION:Given the low level of e-health literacy among patients, implementing national diabetes programs and providing self-management education to patients should be a priority. The use of disease management strategies along with the usage of technologies would enhance patient interaction with electronic tools, which would, in itself, improve e-health literacy.

TI Impact of growth hormone treatment on childhood growth patterns in
   Kermanshah: A retrospective cohort study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Child; human growth hormone; short stature; treatment outcome
ID CHILDREN
AB BACKGROUND: Short stature is a major pediatric concern and a common reason for endocrinology referrals. Although recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) is widely used to treat short stature, its high cost and variable consequences raise concerns about its rational use and long-term effectiveness. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study examined medical records of 260 children aged 3-15 years who received rhGH therapy in Kermanshah between March 2021 and March 2022. Attrition occurred due to physician decision, patient unwillingness to continue treatment, or incomplete records, leaving 54 patients eligible for analysis. This attrition highlights a source of selection bias and limits the generalizability of findings. Growth parameters were assessed across three treatment stages. Pearson correlation and repeated measures ANOVA were performed using SPSS version 22 (P < 0.05). RESULTS: The final cohort included 34 girls and 20 boys with a mean age of approximately 10.5 years. Repeated measures analysis demonstrated a significant increase in mean height z-score from the first to the third treatment stage. Pearson correlation showed no significant association between rhGH dose and growth response. Financial constraints and physician decisions were the main reasons for dropout. CONCLUSION: rhGH therapy improved children's growth parameters independent of dosage intensity. However, the high dropout rate highlights the need for cautious interpretation of the results, as selection bias may have affected the observed results. Transparent reporting of dropout patterns and enhanced financial and clinical support systems are essential to promote equitable access to therapy and strengthen the validity and applicability of future research.

TI Exploring Psychological Factors Affecting the Success of Online Learning
   in Higher Education in Indonesia
SO ONLINE LEARNING
LA English
DT Article
DE Online learning success; emotional intelligance; self-efficacy; self
   motivation; well-being
ID SELF-EFFICACY; STUDENT SATISFACTION; PERCEPTIONS; MOTIVATION; COMMUNITY;
   INQUIRY
AB Online learning in higher education in Indonesia continues to encounter substantial challenges, particularly marked by declining student engagement, increased dropout rates, and the emergence of academic burnout. A shocking phenomenon is the widespread perception of learner apathy, where students demonstrate minimal motivation, reduced participation, and a sense of emotional disconnection from the learning process. These psychological obstacles often undermine the potential of online learning, even when supported by adequate technological infrastructure. Despite these hurdles, online learning remains a necessary and strategic mode of education, especially in bridging geographical disparities across the Indonesian archipelago. Therefore, this study aimed to explore the psychological factors affecting online learning success, including emotional intelligence (EI), psychological well-being (PWB), self-efficacy (SE), and self-motivation (MO), which are believed to be critical in enhancing student engagement and learning outcomes. Engaging 1,052 students in Yogyakarta, the research examined these variables' relationships with online learning success. Online data collection via Google Forms was utilized, with analysis conducted through Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), tested via path analysis and bootstrap. Results indicated that EI, PWB, SE, and MO significantly and positively influenced online learning success. Particularly, MO emerged as an indirect mediator, influencing PWB and SE, thereby enhancing overall online learning effectiveness. This study is pivotal for understanding psychological factors in Indonesian online learning, offering insights into how MO can bolster PWB and SE, ultimately contributing to online learning success. These findings lay a foundation for refining online learning systems, aiming for a more effective and motivating learning environment in the future.

TI Models of Multiculturalism-Based School Ideology: The Reconstructive
   Findings from Indonesia
SO QUALITATIVE RESEARCH IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Indonesia; multiculturalism; school ideology
ID EDUCATION; COMPLEX
AB This study examines the ideology of multiculturalism in school management by reconstructing practices from three distinct educational institutions in Malang, Indonesia. These schools, with diverse approaches to applying multicultural principles, serve as case studies to explore how multiculturalism can be holistically integrated into school management, curriculum, and culture. SNL Public School merges military and civilian education to create a multicultural learning environment; SP Private School fosters inclusivity and social entrepreneurship for marginalized students; and TIB Islamic School blends Islamic values with multicultural principles to encourage religious and cultural harmony. TI The Voice from Indonesia: A Qualitative Exploration of Grit among
   Indonesian School Counsellors
SO QUALITATIVE RESEARCH IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Grit; school counsellors; career sustainability; professional
   resilience; Indonesia
ID SCALE; PERSEVERANCE
AB Grit, characterized by a combination of consistent interest and persistence towards long-term goals, is increasingly recognized as an important factor in professional career success. However, research on grit among school counsellors is limited, especially in Indonesia, where counsellors face unique cultural and systemic challenges. This study examines the factors that influence grit in school counsellors that persist in their profession despite the complexities of education in Indonesia. A qualitative approach was used in this study with semi-structured interviews with seven participants who were selected based on gender representation, work experience, and school type. The thematic analysis revealed six main themes that influenced grit: intrinsic motivation, social support, professional motivation, work environment, resource constraints, and personal coping strategies. These findings emphasize the importance of the interaction between individual resilience and systemic support when building grit. The practical implications of this study include the development of professional development programs and institutional policies to improve the career sustainability and resilience of school counsellors, which will ultimately improve the quality of counselling services in Indonesia.

ID INTIMATE PARTNER VIOLENCE; WOMEN
AB Violence among adolescents is a current public health issue. The present study explores the frequency, directionality, typology and contexts of violence among adolescents in secondary schools from a gender perspective and from the point of view of teachers. A qualitative methodology was used, which triangulated 23 individual in-depth interviews and five focus groups, with a total of 53 teachers from the Community of Madrid (Spain). The results obtained indicate that violence between boys or boys towards girls, verbal abuse, and violence over social media, were the most frequent manifestations. Differences in violence were identified according to the gender of the students, finding that physical violence was more frequent in boys and verbal violence in girls. The role of gender in these behaviours and the consequences and implications for schools are discussed.

   Creative Methodology
SO QUALITATIVE RESEARCH IN EDUCATION
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Inclusive education; personalized learning; universal design for
   learning; design thinking
AB Inclusive education is often confused with approaches derived from special education, as it is reduced to differential treatment towards certain groups considered different, thus requiring an adapted curriculum. TI Integrating STEAM in Early Childhood Education Classrooms: A Reflexive
   Content Analysis of Teachers' Experiences
SO QUALITATIVE RESEARCH IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE STEAM; early childhood education; preschool educators; reflexive content
   analysis
ID SCHOOL
AB Early childhood education plays a crucial role in fostering children's curiosity, creativity, and foundational competences in science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics (STEAM). However, European policies promoting STEAM and digital literacy from preschool onwards have not yet been fully translated into classroom practices that are developmentally appropriate for preschool children. This study explored preschool teachers' experiences integrating STEAM and digital technologies to identify pedagogical and didactic elements that can inform the design of an assessment tool for educators. Using a reflexive content analysis of six teacher interviews conducted in Spain and Germany, five analytical categories were established: pedagogical elements, teacher education, STEAM materials, educational technology, and evaluation processes. Results showed that teachers emphasized child-centred, hands-on approaches, cautious and purposeful use of digital tools, and predominantly observational assessment methods. They also reported fragmented professional training and a lack of structured evaluation instruments. Unlike previous studies that mainly describe barriers to STEAM implementation, this work contributes by identifying teacher-derived pedagogical indicators that can guide the development of a STEAM assessment framework based on Montessori pedagogy and aligned with European early education objectives.

TI Emotional Intelligence in Action: How Leading Teachers in the Maldives
   Resolve Conflict, Sustain Self-Awareness, and Motivate Peers
SO RESEARCH IN EDUCATIONAL ADMINISTRATION & LEADERSHIP
LA English
DT Article
DE emotional intelligence; leading teacher; conflict resolution; teacher
   motivation; self-awareness
ID PRINCIPALS
AB Emotional Intelligence is widely recognized as a critical leadership competency in education, influencing teacher wellbeing, and organizational effectiveness. In the Maldivian education system, Senior Management Team face ongoing challenges such as classroom conflicts, low teacher morale, and emotionally demanding work environments. Despite increasing attention to EQ, limited research has examined how leading teachers enact EQ in their everyday leadership practices within this context. This study addresses this gap by exploring how leading teachers apply EQ to manage conflicts, sustain self-awareness, and motivate teachers experiencing low morale. A qualitative phenomenological design was selected to gain a deep, experiential understanding of how leading teachers subjectively interpret and navigate emotional dynamics in real-time. The study explored the lived experiences of 17 purposively selected leading teachers, a sample size aligning with qualitative guidelines and sufficient for reaching data saturation. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analysed using thematic analysis guided by Braun and Clarke's (2006) framework. The findings indicate that for conflict management (RQ1), leading teachers rely on empathy and active listening, to sustain self-awareness (RQ2), they utilize mindful self-reflection and emotional regulation, and to motivate peers (RQ3), they apply recognition and compassionate flexibility. These findings extend transformational leadership theory by providing a culturally contextualized framework that maps Goleman's EQ model onto the collectivist,community-oriented dynamics of small island developing states. Future research should examine longitudinal effects of EQ-based leadership interventions and culturally responsive adaptations across diverse educational settings.

TI Training University Teaching Staff In ICT And Disability. Perceptions Of
   Technical Staff And Heads Of University Units Providing Support To
   Students With Disabilities.
SO REVISTA DE EDUCACION INCLUSIVA
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Special education; higher education; ICT; disability; education and
   training
ID HIGHER-EDUCATION; ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY
AB This study analyses the training of university teaching staff in Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) for working with students with disabilities at Andalusian universities. A qualitative methodology was used, based on semi-structured interviews with 16 professionals responsible for support services and technological resources at various public and private higher education institutions. The aim was to ascertain their perceptions of the level of digital competence among teaching staff, the existence of training experiences, the benefits of ICT for students with functional diversity, and the main barriers that hinder teacher training. The results show a broad consensus in recognising that ICT promotes accessibility, autonomy, and academic and social integration for students with disabilities. However, there is a gap between teachers' willingness and their actual preparation: most lack specific training in the application of inclusive technologies and require individualised guidance for each case. In addition, training experiences are scarce, uneven and, in many centres, dependent on specific initiatives. The main barriers identified are lack of time, low awareness, limited availability of activities and the perception of low demand. The study concludes that, in order to move towards an inclusive university, solid institutional policies and ongoing training plans are needed that integrate digital accessibility and universal design for learning as strategic elements of educational quality and equity.

TI Response of the Spanish Educational System to Sexual Violence against
   Children
SO REVISTA INTERNACIONAL DE EDUCACION PARA LA JUSTICIA SOCIAL
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Education; Sexual violence; Sexual assault; Child abuse; Children's
   rights
AB The protection of minors from sexual violence is a key challenge for the Spanish educational system. This study examines the educational response of the 17 Spanish Autonomous Communities through a qualitative documentary analysis of 19 official protocols and guidelines. The aim is to compare their main characteristics and conceptualizations, as well as the functions assigned to educational guidance practitioners. Regional documents in force were reviewed and coded around three categories: description of documents, crimes against sexual freedom, and functions of educational guidance. The results reveal considerable heterogeneity among the analyzed protocols, limited updating to current legislation, unequal incorporation of a gender perspective, and scarce inclusion of specific indicators for detecting child sexual violence. The functions of educational guidance are often vaguely defined and interinstitutional coordination is weak. The study concludes that it is necessary to develop specific and updated protocols, with unified criteria, clear indicators and a better defined role for educational guidance, in order to strengthen prevention, early detection and intervention in cases of sexual violence against children and adolescents.

TI Axiological Study of SDG 4: Quality Education
SO REVISTA INTERNACIONAL DE EDUCACION PARA LA JUSTICIA SOCIAL
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Values; Content; Integral education; Quality education; Sustainable
   Development Goals
ID VALUES EDUCATION
AB The documents that regulate or enact educational actions, whether at the local or global level, must take into account a integral perspective if they aim to guarantee quality education. For this reason, Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG 4) in the 2030 Agenda is analyzed from an axiological perspective, evaluating the values which are incorporated, and those omitted in its conception of "quality education". The methodology applies the qualitative content analysis technique, allowing to address the three objectives: to identify the explicit and implicit values in SDG 4, to establish their hierarchy, and to determine their impact on educational systems. The results show that the 2030 Agenda prioritizes moral values, followed by instrumental values, with lesser representation of intellectual, social, and ecological values. The study highlights the absence of fundamental values for integral education: affective, individual, aesthetic, and religious values. Additionally, the low representation of ecological values is striking, considering that sustainability is a central pillar of the 2030 Agenda. Results raise questions about the person underlying model in SDG 4, and about the ability of this international framework to encompass all dimensions of human development.

TI Inclusion or Covert Exclusion? Prejudice towards Refugees among
   Secondary and Upper Secondary Education Students
SO REVISTA INTERNACIONAL DE EDUCACION PARA LA JUSTICIA SOCIAL
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Classical and conditioned prejudice; Refugees; PAAS; Compulsory
   secondary education; Upper secondary education
ID METHODOLOGIES
AB In the current context, shaped by migration crises and growing political polarisation, it is essential to understand prejudice towards refugees, especially in adolescence, a key stage in the formation of values. Research on prejudice among school students remains limited in the Spanish context. This quantitative, non-experimental, cross-sectional study examined the presence of classical and conditioned prejudice, as well as attitudes towards refugees, in a sample of 200 Secondary and Upper Secondary Education students. The PAAS (Prejudice Against Asylum Seekers Scale) questionnaire was adapted to Spanish, and an attitude measurement questionnaire was used as a complementary instrument. Differences were analysed according to gender, academic year and other sociodemographic variables. The findings reveal higher levels of conditioned prejudice than classical prejudice. Attitudes towards refugees are negatively correlated with both types of prejudice. Statistically significant differences were identified according to gender and educational stage, with male students and those in upper secondary education showing higher levels of prejudice. These results highlight the need for educational interventions that address subtle prejudices and promote critical thinking, empathy and intercultural education from the early stages of the education system.

TI Evaluation of Teaching for Global Readiness using Mixed Methods
SO REVISTA INTERNACIONAL DE EDUCACION PARA LA JUSTICIA SOCIAL
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Global citizenship education; Global competence; Teacher appraisal;
   Teacher training; Mixed-methods research
ID COMPETENCE; EDUCATION
AB The need to prepare students for life in a global society is driving the review of, and improvements to teaching practices. This mixed-methods study adapts the Teaching for Global Readiness Scale (TGRS) for use in Spanish and analyses the factors influencing teaching for the development of Global Competence (GC). In the quantitative phase, the scale was administered to teachers at different levels of education (N = 326), alongside the personal GC subscale, in order to validate it. In the qualitative phase, nine teachers were interviewed to provide further insight into the results. The analyses confirm the structural consistency of TGRS and show solid reliability. The Intercultural Experience dimension requires further attention in future studies. Qualitative results confirm that science teachers face difficulties in integrating this teaching approach, although feasible experiences are identified which highlight the key role of interdisciplinary work.

TI Global Citizenship Education: An Analysis of Discourses Among
   Professionals
SO REVISTA INTERNACIONAL DE EDUCACION PARA LA JUSTICIA SOCIAL
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Global citizenship education; Discourse; Education professionals; Youth
   Participation; Local-global
AB Global Citizenship Education (GCE) has emerged as a broad and contested concept shaped by multiple perspectives that influence both its conceptualizations and practices. This study brings that debate to the context of the Principality of Asturias (Spain) with the aim of analyzing how different professionals implement GCE in their work with young people. Drawing on Pashby et al.'s (2020) framework, which identifies six discourses on GCE, a discourse analysis was conducted based on interviews with 20 professionals. The results show that there are differences in the conceptualization of GCE, often linked to participation as a form of activism and resistance. They also reveal that, in a context such as Asturias, characterized by a strong participatory tradition, the local dimension serves as the starting point for addressing global citizenship issues. Although focusing on the local contributes to fostering a situated form of citizenship, it can also hinder broader engagement with global perspectives. Finally, the study highlights discursive differences between formal and non-formal education when approaching GCE, emphasizing a growing presence of critical and post-critical discourses in the social sphere and neoliberal elements within the school context.

TI Pedagogy of Hope in Times of Global Crises
SO REVISTA INTERNACIONAL DE EDUCACION PARA LA JUSTICIA SOCIAL
LA English
DT Article
DE Civil society organisations; Eco-anxiety; Global citizenship; Pedagogy;
   Social change
AB Global citizenship education provides a valuable approach to address today's global crises. International policymakers and a range of academics have enabled global citizenship to become an influential field within education. This theoretically oriented article examines critical pedagogy, the challenges educators face and their role in a world in crisis, and the contribution of the critical global citizenship education approach to build a distinctive and useful vision that promotes social transformation. Using a pedagogy of hope, inspired by the writings of Freire and Giroux, an approach to learning can inspire educators to see education as a vehicle for social change. Within this general framework, two grassroots development education organisations in England through their projects provide evidence of pedagogy of hope in practice. Both share a common focus on using art to express diversity and build community, acknowledging issues-such as eco-anxiety-that affect us personally and can paralyze us, using these as catalysts for change, and creating a framework for understanding reality that allows us to move from the local to the global. Such an approach can inspire educators to see their role as providing a way forward that not only helps address today's global challenges but also engages learners.

TI Realising the Right to Participate: Education for Global Citizenship
   with an Inclusive Approach
SO REVISTA INTERNACIONAL DE EDUCACION PARA LA JUSTICIA SOCIAL
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Global citizenship education; Inclusive research; Youth participatory
   research; Youth as researchers of global challenges; SDG Agenda
AB The results of publicly funded research are presented. The main objective is to realise the right to an education for global citizenship that enables all people, without exception, can access knowledge, skills and educational experiences that enable them to understand and act in the complex global world in which we live, based on the principles of equality, a culture of peace, the value of diversity and sustainable development, in line with the SDG Agenda (target 4.7). Three case studies are described in which work has been carried out with groups that have historically had limited voice and agency, as well as fewer opportunities for social participation, using a research methodology that enables participants to take on the role of researchers of global issues. The results present the working context, research process, and topics, as well as the global lessons learned (both by young people and professionals) in each case. The conclusion is that there is a need to continue developing research methodologies that expand the possibilities for real and effective participation by all people, realizing their role as agents of social change.

TI Faculty and Student Perceptions of Inclusion: Validation of a
   Questionnaire in Higher Education
SO REVISTA INTERNACIONAL DE EDUCACION PARA LA JUSTICIA SOCIAL
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Questionnaire; Higher education; Inclusion; Social justice; Validation
ID DIVERSITY; JUSTICE; EQUITY
AB Currently, universities must make progress toward social justice and the promotion of inclusive educational environments. To this end, it is useful to have instruments that make it possible to estimate the level of inclusion. The objectives of this study were to adapt one of the Index for Inclusion questionnaires to the university context and to assess the level of inclusion of a higher education institution using the adapted instrument. Through a process of expert validation and piloting, the Inclusion Questionnaire for Higher Education (IQHE) was validated. The IQHE maintains the three dimensions and six sections of the original instrument on which it is based and displays high validity and reliability. Furthermore, its application made it possible to identify strengths, weaknesses, and areas of unawareness within the educational community, which we report in our findings. As projections of the study, it is proposed that the designed instrument be applied to students and faculty in other higher education institutions to support its validity. In addition, it is suggested to integrate the use of focus groups to further explore existing barriers in higher education contexts.

TI Attention to Diversity in Basic Vocational Training Cycle
SO REVISTA INTERNACIONAL DE EDUCACION PARA LA JUSTICIA SOCIAL
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Attention to diversity; Social justice; Teacher commitment; Cooperative
   work; Community development
ID STUDENTS
AB Basic Vocational Training Courses (CFGB) carry out commendable work in addressing early school leaving (ESL). The general objective of this research is to analyze the opinions of teachers at CFGBs in the Basque Country regarding the measures, resources, and strategies used to address student diversity. After contacting the 81 schools that make up the population, data was collected using a validated Likert-type questionnaire from 238 professionals from 52 schools. Their selection was both opinion-based and voluntary. The distribution of schools by province and ownership guarantees the external validity of the results. The specific measures most valued by teachers include personalized tutoring, the adaptation of objectives, content, activities, and assessment criteria for students with academic problems, the development of personalized work plans and cooperative learning in the classroom. Teacher commitment to attention to diversity is correlated with the four dimensions of the instrument detailed in the methodology. In the medium term, it is necessary to design an action plan that promotes collaboration and coordination between different educational and social institutions.

TI The School Playground as a Critical Space for Dynamics of Inclusion vs.
   Social Exclusion among Peers
SO REVISTA INTERNACIONAL DE EDUCACION PARA LA JUSTICIA SOCIAL
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Playground; School inclusion; Diversity; Recess
ID SPECIAL NEEDS; CHILDREN; EDUCATION; PERCEPTIONS; PLAY
AB In the realm of education, less formal and structured environments, such as school playgrounds, are often the most overlooked. Despite this, what happens during recess significantly impacts students' overall school experience, whether positively or negatively. Previous studies have shown that active participation in these spaces helps reduce social exclusion and fosters a greater sense of belonging. This article aims to contribute to the discussion about the role of school playgrounds, their potential, and the challenges they pose in promoting social inclusion among students, regardless of abilities, ethnic background, or socioeconomic status. Through focus groups conducted with members of the educational community (teachers, families, and social organizations), the study seeks to describe and analyze the functionality of playgrounds and explore possible improvements. Focus groups were held in Sevilla, C & oacute;rdoba, and Ja & eacute;n. The results reveal a general consensus on the importance of playgrounds, not only as spaces for rest but also as environments for acquiring social skills, resolving conflicts, and fostering tolerance and cooperation. However, widespread dissatisfaction with playground management was also evident, highlighting a lack of material and human resources dedicated to their improvement. The study underscores instances of rejection and social exclusion within school playgrounds.

TI From Development Education to Global Justice Education: Lessons and
   Challenges from Educational Projects in Barcelona
SO REVISTA INTERNACIONAL DE EDUCACION PARA LA JUSTICIA SOCIAL
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Global justice education; Development education; Global citizenship;
   Global south; Diagnosis of educational policies
AB This article analyzes the transition from Development Education (DE) to Global Justice Education (GJE) through the case of the city of Barcelona. In a global context of interdependent crises, GJE is consolidating as a transformative educational approach driven by administrations, social and educational organizations that are reshaping their practices to build a critical, inclusive, and globally committed citizenship. A mixed-methods design was applied, combining the quantitative analysis of 277 projects funded by the Barcelona City Council between 2018 and 2022 with a qualitative approach based on participatory discussion groups involving organizations, public administrations, and universities. The findings reveal a paradigm shift in educational practices, characterized by thematic diversification, the strengthening of territorial collaborations, and the incorporation of intersectoral and global perspectives. Challenges remain in assessing social impact, communication, and maintaining connections with the Global South. The Barcelona experience stands out as a significant example for understanding how organizations are building this new educational paradigm in practice, offering key insights and tensions that contribute to the advancement of Global Justice Education.

TI Exploring Resistance towards Feminism among Secondary School Students:
   Three Case Studies in Public Institutes in Catalonia
SO REVISTA INTERNACIONAL DE EDUCACION PARA LA JUSTICIA SOCIAL
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Feminism; High school; Students; Resistance; Coeducation
AB The objective of this article is to analyze the resistance towards feminism that is manifested among high school students. To this end, three case studies have been carried out with an ethnographic approach in educational institutions in Catalonia. The information obtained, which includes participant observation and a detailed diary, has been analyzed through content analysis. Four major examples of resistance emerge from the results: confrontation, denial, loss of privileges and maintenance of the status quo. These patterns of resistance not only reveal individual attitudes, but also reflect broader social and cultural dynamics that perpetuate gender inequalities. It concludes by linking these different manifestations with a reflection on the need to develop coeducation from an intersectional approach. To achieve this, it is essential to apply a perspective that considers the multiple dimensions of identity that affect the student body, such as gender, race, class, sexual orientation, among others. Therefore, the different scenarios identified are not only seen as challenges, but also as opportunities to transform the educational context from a social justice perspective.

TI Global Citizenship Education: Teachers' Perception and Commitment in
   their Teaching Practice
SO REVISTA INTERNACIONAL DE EDUCACION PARA LA JUSTICIA SOCIAL
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Education for sustainable development; Education for global citizenship;
   Teachers; Formal education; Transformative education
ID SCHOOLS
AB Education from a Global Citizenship perspective is conceived as a process aimed at shaping critical citizens capable of rebuilding a fairer society. This transformative process cannot be understood without recognising the role of teachers. Consequently, this study analyses teachers' perceptions of social and educational realities, identifying the changes that occur in their teaching practice following their participation in Global Citizenship Education (GCE) projects. Using a quantitative approach, a descriptive cross-sectional study and an inferential analysis were carried out using a questionnaire completed by 200 early years and primary school teachers in Arag & oacute;n. The results show that teachers are sensitive to major social issues. After participating in GCE projects, they perceive themselves as more involved, committed and as agents of change. These changes are also evident in their practice, where age, experience and training in GCE influence practices of participation, coordination and synergies with the community. Transformative education becomes a challenge, in which teachers need support, coordination and training so that it translates into greater impact through socio-educational practice.

TI IMMIGRANT PARENTS FROM KOSOVO ON HELPING THEIR CHILDREN WITH SCHOOLWORK
SO SODOBNA PEDAGOGIKA-JOURNAL OF CONTEMPORARY EDUCATIONAL STUDIES
LA English
DT Article
DE immigrant parents from Kosovo; school-immigrant parent cooperation;
   parental assistance with schoolwork; children of immigrant parents;
   academic achievement
ID INVOLVEMENT; EDUCATION; BARRIERS
AB Parental involvement in their children's education is an important factor in learning and social development and is widely recognised as a principle of effective educational practice. However, little research has focused on the involvement of immigrant parents in supporting their children with schoolwork, particularly in the context of the linguistic, social, and cultural circumstances of immigration. This paper examines parents who have immigrated from Kosovo (N = 246) with children attending Slovenian primary schools, analysing the frequency and methods of their assistance with schoolwork. The data analysis shows that in immigrant families from Kosovo, assisting with schoolwork is primarily the responsibility of mothers. Regarding the frequency of assistance, the results indicate that children receive help from parents only a few times a month, from siblings a few times a year, even less often from classmates and professionals outside school, and almost never from an instructor. In terms of the ways parents help their children with schoolwork, the analysis shows that parents often supervise, remind, and encourage their children to learn but rarely become directly involved in the learning process itself (e.g. studying together, checking the child's knowledge, or reading with the child). The academic success of children who had received numerical grades was reported by parents to be relatively low (M = 2.64), with approximately one-fifth of parents stating that their child had repeated a school grade. When interpreting the results, it is important to consider the broader structural and sociocultural circumstances that may affect parents' opportunities to be involved in their children's schoolwork.

TI Understanding embodied learning: A qualitative study with pedagogy
   students in Croatia
SO SODOBNA PEDAGOGIKA-JOURNAL OF CONTEMPORARY EDUCATIONAL STUDIES
LA English
DT Article
DE body-mind dialectic; learning experiences; undergraduate student
   perspective; studentled tour
ID SPACE; PERSPECTIVES
AB The dialectical relationship between body and mind in learning requires a re-examination of both teaching practices and the broader aims of education. Although studies have consistently demonstrated the benefits of embodied approaches for deeper and more sustainable learning, these approaches remain insufficiently integrated into educational practice. This gap highlights the need to consider how future pedagogues (and teachers) can be supported in developing these approaches during their initial education. The aim of this study was to gain insight into how students double majoring in pedagogy understand embodied learning within the context of initial teacher and pedagogue education in Croatia. Three methods were employed: analysis of study programmes, a student-led classroom tour, and a focus group with eight undergraduate students double majoring in pedagogy. Data sources included recordings, notes, and photographs from the tour, as well as transcriptions of the focus group discussion, all of which were subjected to thematic analysis. The findings revealed that students recognised embodied learning as valuable but continued to perceive the classroom space as sedentary. The study also identified challenges related to students' bodily self-perception in relation to learning and movement, which may influence their ability to apply embodied learning approaches in practice. Particular attention should therefore be given to preparing future pedagogues and teachers through experiential learning situated within their sociocultural context as a necessary foundation for meaningful changes in practice.

AB This study aimed to describe and evaluate a newly developed self-experiential seminar designed for students of special education at higher education institutions. TI Integrating virtual reality painting practice into foundational drawing
   education: Students' learning experiences and outcomes
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATION THROUGH ART
LA English
DT Article
DE Tilt Brush; immersive learning; sense of presence; technology
   acceptance; model; perceived usefulness; perceived ease of use; creative
   thinking; disposition; spatial visualization
ID ACCEPTANCE; WORLDS
AB This study investigates how virtual reality (VR) painting using Tilt Brush can complement foundational drawing education by supporting immersive, spatial and embodied interaction. Using a mixed-methods design, data were collected from university art and design students through surveys (e.g. technology acceptance and presence), an artwork evaluation rubric and semi-structured interviews. Findings indicate that VR environments can enhance students' motivation and engagement through dynamic brush effects and spatial freedom. AB Our collaborative autoethnographic (CAE) inquiry explores what art educators need to know to teach elementary generalists well. We analysed how authors in the United States perceive the challenges and remedies for teaching generalist art methods courses and how our lived experiences support or complicate normalized assumptions about teaching art methods for general educators. TI No-cost graphic design under-represented students and fostering industry
   diversity
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATION THROUGH ART
LA English
DT Article
DE design pedagogy; summer programme; diversity; inclusivity;
   Hispanic-serving institution; portfolio development; creative education
AB This study examines a two-week, no-cost graphic design residency camp for high school students in Texas from historically under-represented racial and ethnic backgrounds, first-generation college-bound students or those who have overcome social or economic hardship. Developed to address diversity gaps in the graphic design industry, the programme served 37 Black, Hispanic/Latino and Indigenous students over three summers. The curriculum focused on conceptual, professional and technical skills through project-based learning, professional interactions and visits to creative organizations. Through analysis of participant surveys and testimonials, we evaluated the programme's effectiveness in building foundational design knowledge and supporting participants' exploration of graphic design as an academic and career option. Results indicated observed improvements in participants' design software proficiency, conceptual understanding and self-assessed creative abilities. Interest in studying graphic design remained stable across the programme (43% at completion), while career interest showed growth from 32% at intake to 46% at completion, with educational and career aspirations converging by the end of the programme. These findings demonstrate promising potential for early intervention programmes to address the critical talent shortage of designers from diverse backgrounds.

TI Academic scientific impact and emerging patterns in research on
   additives, preservatives and asthma: A scientometric analysis
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Asthma; bibliometrics; food additives; preservatives; respiratory
   diseases
AB BACKGROUND:Food additives and preservatives are widely used, but the associations between additives and preservatives and asthma have been hardly investigated. The existing research is limited and scattered and warrants further serious scientific and public health inquiry. To examine scientific literature concerning the relationship between food additives, preservatives and asthma. It identified relevant trends and patterns of global interest and measured academic impact an international collaboration in this area.MATERIAL AND METHODS:A scientometric analysis was conducted covering publications between January 2019 and March 2025. The indicators considered included annual publication growth, cumulative citations, citation indexes, and international collaboration patterns. The search, conducted in the Scopus database, used specific terms and rigorous criteria. The data obtained were analyzed using R Studio software and the bibliometrix tool, complemented with Bradford's and Lotka's laws, collaboration maps, and thematic diagrams.RESULTS:From 2019 to 2025, 22 total documents related to additives, preservatives, and asthma were located, and a modest level of entrance existed in this emerging area of interest. While reflecting a modest area of interest, the average annual growth rate was 5.7%, with 17 citations on average per document. These 175 authors were all involved through collaborations, and only 9% of the publications used international coauthorships. China was the most active countries with 6 articles, with Denmark having the highest weighted impact. The highest average impact was at the University of Zurich, with 83.5 citations per article. The three most frequent keywords in the publications were asthma, allergy, and food additives, which was indicative that the research focused on illnesses of the respiratory system and how they are related to chemical/natural agents and environment.CONCLUSION:The research reports aided in establishing global trends and collaboration patterns when studying modern-day additives and asthma. These reports emphasized not only the need to continue understanding food additives and their impacts on respiratory health but also relevant global scientific activities in this area.

TI Rajasekaran's K-Matrix Criterion and the Foundations of Hadron
   Compositeness
SO RESONANCE-JOURNAL OF SCIENCE EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Hadrons; QCD; scattering amplitudes; unitarity; analyticity
AB Notwithstanding the well-established status of quantum chromodynamics (QCD) as the theory of strong interactions, the internal composition of hadrons remains an open problem. Prof. G. Rajasekaran's (respectfully addressed as Rajaji in the Indian scientific community) work [1], one of the earliest attempts to address this, provided a physically transparent criterion for hadron compositeness using the analytic structure of the 'K-matrix'. He argued that the absence of K-matrix poles is a distinctive signature of dynamically generated states, providing a clean framework to extract hadron compositeness from scattering amplitudes. In this article, we revisit these pioneering ideas by Rajaji [1] and place them in the context of modern developments, including Weinberg's compositeness relations, CDD ambiguity, effective field theory approaches, and contemporary lattice QCD analyses.

TI The Curious Case of a Mosquito Bite
SO RESONANCE-JOURNAL OF SCIENCE EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Mosquito; proboscis; olfaction; antennal lobe
AB Mosquitoes transmit deadly diseases such as malaria, dengue, Chikungunya, and Zika, leading to a significant number of deaths each year. They are often referred to as 'the most dangerous animal on Earth'. Despite this, the stealthy methods employed by mosquitoes for sucking blood and the sensory mechanisms involved in the process were discovered only in the last decade. TI Nonlinear Dynamics of the Double Pendulum: A Computational Analysis of
   Sensitivity, Lyapunov Exponents, and Phase-Space Structure
SO RESONANCE-JOURNAL OF SCIENCE EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Nonlinear dynamics; double pendulam; Lyapunov exponents
AB The double pendulum is a classical model of deterministic chaos, showing extreme sensitivity to initial conditions, all the while specified by fully known classical equations. This first part describes a numerical study of the undamped double pendulum-in Lagrangian form-using high-precision numerical integration with small perturbations in initial conditions resulting in rapid divergence in trajectories. The time-series analysis of trajectories and the computation of the maximal Lyapunov exponent via the two-trajectory method quantifies the divergence. Phase-space portraits can illustrate bounded, but aperiodic, motion with the defining characteristics of nonlinear chaotic systems. All simulations are mounted with open-source Python tools (NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib, and FuncAnimation), allowing for a transparent and pedagogical environment suitable for advanced undergraduates or graduates in the study of classical mechanics and nonlinear dynamics.

TI Markov Processes and Brain Network Hubs
SO RESONANCE-JOURNAL OF SCIENCE EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Brain network hubs; Markov chains; epilepsy
ID CONNECTOME
AB Current concepts of neural networks have emerged over two centuries of progress, beginning with the neural doctrine to the idea of neural cell assemblies. Presently, neural network models involve distributed neural circuits of nodes, hubs, and connections that are dynamic across different states of brain function. Advances in neurophysiology, neuroimaging, and the field of connectomics have given impetus to the application of mathematical concepts of graph theory. Current approaches do have limitations and inconsistencies in the results they achieve. We model the neural network of the brain as a directed graph and attach a matrix (called the Markov matrix) of transition probabilities (determined by the synaptic strengths) to every pair of distinct nodes, giving rise to a discrete Markov process. We postulate that the network hubs are the nodes with the highest probabilities given by the stationary distribution of Markov theory. We also derive a new upper bound for the diameter of a graph in terms of the eigenvalues of the Markov matrix.

TI Scaling Leadership Support: Evidence-Informed Workload Policies for
   Department Chairs in Growing Public Universities
SO JOURNAL OF HIGHER EDUCATION POLICY AND LEADERSHIP STUDIES
LA English
DT Article
DE Leadership Policy; Academic Leadership; Department Chairs; Workload
   Policy; Organizational Design; Leadership Development
AB This study investigates how institutional growth and department size shape department chair leadership effectiveness, providing evidence-based policy recommendations for higher education governing boards, institutional administrators, and policymakers. Drawing on mixed-methods data from 67 chairs and directors at a large U.S. public research university (42% response rate) and follow-up interviews (n=11), the study examines how perceived administrative workload, time pressure, and leadership development needs vary systematically by department size. Findings reveal that chairs of large departments (40+ faculty) face fundamentally different administrative demands than chairs of small departments (<= 20 faculty), while medium-sized units experience disproportionate personnel management challenges. Yet most institutions apply uniform workload policies, course release allocations, and support structures across all department sizes. Chairs overwhelmingly prioritize structural solutions-dedicated administrative staff, streamlined processes, and size-calibrated workload models-over professional development programming. The study provides a policy framework for differentiated leadership support, including scaled course release formulas, size-appropriate administrative staffing models, and targeted leadership development investments. These findings offer governing boards, senior administrators, and state-level policymakers an evidence-based roadmap for designing sustainable academic leadership infrastructure that aligns resources with organizational complexity.

TI The Integration of Micro-Credentials in Higher Education: A Systematic
   Review and a Strategic Reset Model
SO JOURNAL OF HIGHER EDUCATION POLICY AND LEADERSHIP STUDIES
LA English
DT Article
DE Micro-Credentials; Higher Education; Lifelong Learning; Certificate
   Programs; Continuing Education
ID STUDENTS; FORM
AB The rapid digitalization of the labor market has widened the gap between graduate competencies and industry needs, challenging the relevance of traditional higher education degrees. While micro-credentials have emerged as agile solutions to bridge this gap, their integration into formal academic structures remains fragmented and theoretically under-conceptualized. This study aims to analyze the pedagogical, administrative, and legal strategies for integrating micro-credentials into higher education and to identify the barriers hindering this process. A systematic literature review was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, analyzing 81 articles published between 2015 and 2025 in the Web of Science and Scopus databases. The thematic synthesis reveals that while stackable degree models and blockchain-based verification are the most prominent integration strategies, the ecosystem is plagued by a trust deficit among employers and a lack of standardized quality assurance frameworks. Furthermore, the findings highlight a critical tension between the labor market's demand for flexibility and the university's need for academic rigor. Based on these findings, the study proposes a Strategic Reset Model, a five-dimensional framework designed to guide higher educational institutes in transforming from mere content providers into accredited competency hubs.

TI Using Traits of Leadership to Overcome the Challenges of Becoming and
   Being a New Teacher in Ontario
SO JOURNAL OF HIGHER EDUCATION POLICY AND LEADERSHIP STUDIES
LA English
DT Article
DE Early Career Teachers; Self-Study of Teacher Education Practices;
   Teacher Resilience; Mentorship; Leadership in Early Career Teaching;
   Reflective Practice; Teacher Leadership
ID ATTRITION
AB This article details a self-study and collaborative response to an early career teacher (ECT) facing challenges in the first year of teaching. Some of the experiences were so demanding that the ECT considered leaving the profession altogether. It is for this reason that the ECT completed a self-study in the first year of teaching under the guidance of a mentor (a former instructor in their teacher education program). The ECT worked as both an occasional teacher and long term occasional teacher in Ontario, Canada during this study. Each teaching assignment presented different kinds of challenges. Although each experience and the accompanying challenges were unique, all of them were overcome with attention to specific traits of leadership. The use of these traits was explored through a self-study methodology that included daily self-reflection, frequent journaling of experiences, and timely communication with a mentor. This article discusses the greatest challenges the ECT experienced in the first year and the ways in which the ECT overcame them through leadership. The article concludes with system-level recommendations developed from these experiences. It is hoped that the insights herein can be used by other new teachers as they navigate the vicissitudes of teaching themselves.

TI Transdisciplinarity as an Approach to Integrating Environmental
   Education into the Social Sciences
SO REVISTA CIENCIAS PEDAGOGICAS E INNOVACION
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE environmental awareness; environmental education; transdisciplinary
   approach; social sciences education; social studies; basic education;
   curriculum
AB This study examined transdisciplinarity as an approach to integrating environmental education. The objective of the study was to assess the relevance of teaching and learning environmental education from a transdisciplinary perspective in the Social Sciences at the Basic General Education level. The methodology employed a qualitative approach, combining document analysis and interviews. Twenty scientific articles were analyzed, and 10 teachers from the General Basic Education and Higher Education levels of the Ecuadorian educational system were interviewed. The articles identified conceptions of environmental education, as well as technological, visual, recreational, and practical strategies and tools for teaching it, primarily from the Natural Sciences and,to a lesser extent, from other areas such as the Social Sciences and Physical Education. For their part, the teachers emphasized the importance of teaching environmental education through collaborative and transdisciplinary work; however, they identified difficulties in implementing this approach due to teacher training and the current educational curriculum. The study recognizes the relevance of approaching environmental education from the perspective of the Social Sciences with a transdisciplinary focus,which enables the acquisition of knowledge and the development of skills, attitudes, values, and behaviors necessary for making informed decisions and fostering responsible citizenship oriented toward caring for, preserving, and respecting the environment

TI Design and Preliminary Evaluation of a NeuroeducationalGame Applied in
   Higher Education
SO REVISTA CIENCIAS PEDAGOGICAS E INNOVACION
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE active learning; creativity; gamification; instructional materials;
   critical thinking
AB Higher education requires active teaching resources that combine motivation, collaboration, and cognitive challenge. Given the limited use of neuroeducation-based materials in the second year of the Graphic Design program at the Pontifical Catholic University of Ecuador, NeuroLab Play was designed-an educational game with a physical version for implementation and a digital representation as a visual aid. The objective was to design, validate, and implement the resource and to conduct a preliminary assessment of its usability, user satisfaction, and observed evidence of creativity, critical thinking, and collaboration. A sequential mixed-methods approach was applied, first with a cohort of 10 students for exploration and subsequently with a cohort of 23 students across the Manta and Portoviejo campuses for the game's implementation. Rubrics, a semi-structured questionnaire, non-participant observation, and a checklist were used. The results showed that the prototype received positive ratings for usability (3.96-4.57) and satisfaction (3.26-4.57); its implementation provided preliminary evidence to guide improvements. However, due to the study's pilot nature, non-random sampling, and reliance on self-reports, the findings should be interpreted with caution and cannot be generalised. Despite these limitations, the instructional material shows potential for adaptation and transfer to other educational contexts

TI Socio-environmental Practices and Perceptions Surrounding Recycling and
   Their Contributions to Reflective Environmental Education
SO REVISTA CIENCIAS PEDAGOGICAS E INNOVACION
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE social inequality; education for sustainable development; science
   education; community participation; environmental awareness
ID SOCIOSCIENTIFIC ISSUES
AB Recycling is a socio-environmental practice shaped by social representations, economic tensions, and health risks in vulnerable educational contexts where students, families, and informal recyclers interact. The objective of this study was to understand the socio-environmental perceptions and practices associated with recycling in an educational community in the municipality of Duitama, Boyac & aacute;, Colombia. A mixed-methods approach-combining descriptive analysis and case study methods-was employed, involving 23 students and 13 families. Data were collected using a Likert-scale questionnaire and semi-structured interviews; the data were analyzed using MAXQDA 2024 and RStudio software. The results revealed positive views of recycling alongside limited practices, as well as ambivalent perceptions of waste pickers, associated with social stigma and perceived risk. It was concluded that recycling is recognized as a relevant environmental practice, yet one that is subject to social and cultural tensions that affect its everyday adoption.

TI From Traditional to Computational: Teaching and Learning Statistics with
   Jupyter Notebook
SO REVISTA CIENCIAS PEDAGOGICAS E INNOVACION
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE statistics; learning experience; pedagogical innovation; teaching method
AB Learning statistics is challenging when approached in an abstract manner and disconnected from real-world contexts. This research presents a descriptive statisticteaching experience in higher education using Jupyter Notebook with Python libraries and real-world datasets. A case study was conducted with 28 students in the Experimental Sciences, Mathematics, and Physics Education program at a public university in Ecuador. The intervention was structured into three cyclical phases (initiation, development, and closure) and implemented over 10 hours of in-person instruction spread across two weeks. Qualitative analysis of student testimonials revealed that the experience was perceived as innovative and satisfying, promoting understanding of fundamental statistical concepts, the handling of datasets, and the application of visualization techniques. The results suggest that Jupyter Notebook can serve as a relevant pedagogical tool for fostering active and contextualized statistical learning experiences, provided its use is accompanied by appropriate faculty guidance from instructors with basic proficiency in Python and in the design of technology-mediated learning environments

TI Constitutional Analysis of the Principle of Equality and
   Non-Discrimination in Light of Article 115 of the Ecuadorian Labor Code
SO REVISTA CIENCIAS PEDAGOGICAS E INNOVACION
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE constitutional law; labor law; discrimination; equal rights
AB This study analyzed Article 115 of the Ecuadorian Labor Code in relation to the constitutional principle of equality and non-discrimination, with the aim of evaluating the reasonableness of the differential treatment granted to workers and artisan apprentices with regard to employment bonuses. The study adopted a qualitative and documentary approach, based on the analysis of constitutional provisions, labor legislation, specialized legal doctrine, and the case law of the Constitutional Court of Ecuador. The results showed that the principle of equality in the Ecuadorian constitutional order has a substantive dimension that requires an assessment of both the content of the provisions and their practical effects. By applying the criteria of reasonableness and proportionality, it was determined that the exclusion provided for in Article 115 fails to meet the constitutional test, as it affects labor rights without sufficient justification. It is concluded that the provision is incompatible with the principle of equality and non-discrimination, which highlights the need for a regulatory review in accordance with current constitutional standards.

TI Open innovation in SMEs: a systematic review of the context, networks
   and public policies
SO REVISTA CIENCIAS PEDAGOGICAS E INNOVACION
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE government support; interorganizational collaboration; commercialization
   of innovation; business performance; collaborative ecosystems;
   innovation networks
ID MEDIUM ENTERPRISES
AB Research on open innovation in SMEs has expanded significantly over the past decade; however, the field lacks an integrated, theory-grounded synthesis that consolidates recent empirical evidence. This study aims to synthesize the findings and identify dominant thematic subcategories to guide future research. A systematic literature review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA protocol, using publications retrieved from Scopus and WoS between 2021 and 2025; 59 peer-reviewed articles were identified from an initial corpus of 334. The results reveal that empirical research on open innovation in SMEs is predominantly based on longitudinal data and is geographically concentrated in Europe, with contributions from Asia, particularly China and India. At thesame time, studies from the Americas, especially Latin America, are scarce. The synthesis indicates that open innovation improves overall performance in SMEs; its impact is more pronounced in commercialization and market-oriented activities than in initial R&D (Research and Development) processes. The study concludes that open innovation must be understood as a context-dependent and policy-driven phenomenon. It highlights the need for comprehensive public policies and collaborative ecosystems that strengthen SMEs' capacity to participate strategically in open innovation networks.

TI Intercultural Necropolitical Cartography of Dehumanization from the
   Perspective of Interventional Bioethics
SO REVISTA CIENCIAS PEDAGOGICAS E INNOVACION
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE bioethics; intercultural communicative competence; dehumanization;
   cosmopolitan crossroads; the included other; homo sacer-bare life
AB This research report, derived from a doctoral dissertation on complex thinking, examines the global crisis of necropolitical dehumanization evident in the 21st century. The case study examines the ontological expropriation to which a subject deported from the United States was subjected, and considers this subject a third party (T) in the intercultural communicative competence (ICC) of foreign languages and cultures (FLC). In this process, all his political rights were stripped away: from homo sacer, he became bare life. Through ontologies of domination calculated by artificial intelligence (AI), the bioethical destruction to which he was subjected was established. The analysis was conducted based on an intercultural necropolitical cartography, in which intercultural communicative competence was found to be trapped at the Kantian cosmopolitan crossroads, an anachronistic structure in the face of the dehumanization of the current century.

TI Redesigning corporate learning through ICT and user experience: an
   exploratory mixed-methods evaluation of the user-centred CLEM as a
   strategic tool
SO DIGITAL EDUCATION REVIEW
LA English
DT Article
DE Corporate learning; Digital transformation; Mixed methods study;
   Artificial intelligence; Return on investment modelling; User experience
ID AGREEMENT
AB Digital transformation has redefined corporate training by integrating information and communication technologies (ICTs) and user experience (UX), with artificial intelligence (AI) functioning as a sophisticated enabling technology rather than a standalone pedagogical approach. However, structural challenges related to the digital divide, cultural resistance, and the ethical management of data persist within these digital learning ecosystems. This study seeks to critically evaluate prevailing digital methodologies (such as microlearning, gamification, and adaptive learning) to formulate a strategically integrated Corporate Learning Experience Model (CLEM). The goal is to assess the model's preliminary effectiveness through an exploratory pilot study and establish realistic return on investment (ROI) projections. This study, employing an exploratory mixed-methods research design, integrates a systematic literature review, following the PRISMA 2020 statement, with empirical validation. After examining 312 records, 45 peer-reviewed studies, primarily published between 2010 and 2025, were included for a thematic meta-analysis. This theoretical synthesis was triangulated with four business case studies and a quasi-experimental pilot validation with 48 employees of a digital consulting firm. The analysis identified five key strategic pillars: AI-powered personalisation, microlearning, gamification, workflow-based learning, and predictive analytics. Preliminary results from the pilot study indicated a 62% increase in knowledge retention and an 88% module completion rate. Based on these exploratory findings, the projected financial model suggests a potential three-year cumulative return on investment (ROI) of approximate to 4,943%, although these results are highly dependent on organisational maturity and inclusive implementation. Integrating ICT and UX through a user-centred framework, such as CLEM, improves the efficiency and impact of organisational training. However, its sustainable adoption requires ethical design and operational impact metrics that balance technological innovation with digital justice and employee well-being. It is crucial that technology complements human-centred learning principles without replacing fundamental pedagogical frameworks.

TI Rethinking Workplace Training: Artificial Intelligence, Digital
   Ecosystems, and Emerging Talent Development Practices
SO DIGITAL EDUCATION REVIEW
LA English
DT Article
DE workplace training; artificial intelligence; digital ecosystems;
   personalized learning; microlearning
ID METAANALYSIS
AB The landscape of workplace training is undergoing a radical transformation, driven by the powerful convergence of advan-ced technologies, evolving workforce expectations, and the imperative need for organizational agility. This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the forces reshaping talent development, with a specific focus on the catalytic role of Artificial Intelligence (AI), the integration into holistic digital ecosystems, and the emergence of innovative learning practices. Unlike previous narrative reviews, this study adopts a transparent methodological approach based on a systematic examination of peer-reviewed literature, complemented by industry case studies where they provide unique empirical insights. Through an extensive review of existing studies, this article argues that the traditional, standardized approach to corporate training is rapidly becoming obsolete. We propose a future-oriented model wherein AI personalizes learning pathways, digital ecosystems provide seamless access to knowledge, and emerging practices such as microlearning and gamification significantly enhance learner engagement and skill transfer. The synthesized data from peer-reviewed sources indicates substantial improvements in course completion rates, knowledge retention, and Return on Investment (ROI) when these strategies are implemented effectively, although effect sizes are often more modest than those claimed in non-academic reports. The discussion critically addresses significant challenges, including the digital divide, ethical concerns surrounding AI data usage, and cultural resistance to change. The conclusion underscores the necessity for organizations-and educational institutions alike-to adopt a continuous learning mindset, invest in robust digital infrastructure, and develop inclusive change management strategies to thrive in the digital age.

TI Personalisation and Predictive Insights: Applied AI Strategies in Modern
   Learning Technologies
SO DIGITAL EDUCATION REVIEW
LA English
DT Article
DE Applied Artificial Intelligence; Personalisation; Predictive Analytics;
   Learning Management Systems; Lear-ning Experience Platforms
ID ANALYTICS
AB When companies must grapple with ever-faster technological shifts and changing skill requirements, the classic, one-size-fits-all models of workplace learning systems fall short in meeting the needs of a diverse workforce and of predicting per-formance paths. We study how applied AI strategies, collaborative filtering, decision-tree classification, and neural network prediction are implemented in the three leading corporate learning technologies (Learning Management Systems-LMS, Learning Experience Platforms-LXP, and Talent Management Platforms-TMP). The primary aims include quantifying the impact of AI-enabled personalised learning on individual learner engagement and satisfaction, validating the predictive power of AI models for forecasting individual learning outcomes, and comparing the effectiveness of AI applications across different platform archetypes. We employed a mixed-methods quasi-experimental design, collaborating with three multina-tional organisations (technology, finance, and healthcare), with three employees from each organisation assigned to test one of the platforms (N = 450). Detailed system logs (page views, content accesses, quiz attempts), completion rates, and standardised post-training assessment scores were collected over six months, along with pre-and post-intervention survey responses (satisfaction with content, perceived relevance). Openended survey questions and focus group interviews pro-vided qualitative insight into AI usability and recommendation quality. The microservice-based AI modules were integrated through platform APIs with a nightly batch-processing pipeline. Collaborative filtering applied user-item matrix factorisation to generate top-five course recommendations; decision-tree classifiers (CART) predicted the likelihood of completing a module based on early engagement metrics; and feed-forward multilayer perceptrons predicted post-assessment per-formance by incorporating features (demographics, prior performance, and interaction metrics). Models were trained on the first three months of data, validated in the fourth month, and deployed in the fifth and sixth months to enable real-time personalisation and prediction. Findings suggest that incorporating AI significantly enhanced learning performance. Users who received AI recommendations (n = 225) achieved 22.1 higher percentile points of active Usage compared to controls (n = 225), t(448) = 24.6, p < .001, and the proportion of passed modules increased from 62.4% to 81.7%, chi(2)(1, N = 450) = 48.9, p < .001. Neural network predictors achieved a mean absolute error of 0.12 on normalised assessment scores, while decision-tree models achieved an F1-score of 0.87 for completion predictions. The top-five hit rate for collaborative filtering recommendations was 0.78. Survey satisfaction scores were higher among AI recipients (M = 4.5/5) than controls (M = 3.8/5), F(1, 448) = 182.7, p < .001. Platform-specific analyses indicated that LXPs showed a significant increase in voluntary engagement (Delta = +28.4 percentile points). TMPs provided the best support for aligning training with career de-velopment milestones (74% agree/strongly agree vs. 58% for LMS and 62% for LXP). Ethical aspects, such as informed consent, data anonymisation, and GDPR compliance, have been carefully managed. These results demonstrate that im-plemented AI approaches can enhance personalisation and the predictive capabilities of workplace learning technologies.
   The research provides a validated architecture for AI production, including modular microservices, transparent recommen-dation interfaces, and model retraining pipelines. It offers evidence-based suggestions to practitioners concerning platform choice and model strategy.
