TI Development and Qualitative Evaluation of A Biomimicry-Enriched
   Engineering Design-Based Teaching Module on The Sound and Its Properties
   Unit
SO JURNAL PENDIDIKAN FISIKA INDONESIA-INDONESIAN JOURNAL OF PHYSICS
   EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE biomimicry; engineering design-based teaching; levels of biomimicry;
   sound; STEM education
ID STUDENTS; STEM
AB This study proposes and investigates a biomimicry-enriched, engineering design-based teaching approach for physics. Grounded in situated learning theory, the approach aims to enhance student comprehension and interest by connecting abstract concepts to real-world problem-solving and daily life, a crucial mandate in physics education research. The focus of this research is on the "sound and its properties" unit. The implementation was conducted over 22 class hours, during which students participated in nature-inspired engineering design cycles comprising stages such as problem definition, imagining solutions, identifying sources of inspiration, and modelling. Using a qualitative research design, the study analyzed data from 57 sixth-grade students in Ankara, T & uuml;rkiye. Qualitative data, collected via students' cooperative group activity sheets, required students to identify biological sources and map similarities between nature and their designs. These data were analyzed through inductive document and content analysis to categorize typical designs and the specific levels of biomimetic mimicry achieved by the groups. The findings provide detailed insights into the students' application of physics principles to design nature-inspired engineering solutions related to sound and its properties.

TI Correlation Between AI Usage and Students' Perceptions in Learning
   Kirchhoff's Law at Senior High School in South Jakarta
SO JURNAL PENDIDIKAN FISIKA INDONESIA-INDONESIAN JOURNAL OF PHYSICS
   EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Artificial Intelligence; Kirchhoff's Law; student perception;
   correlation; physics learning
AB The Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Physics learning is growing. However, the correlation between AI usage and supporting students' understanding of basic electrical concepts, such as Kirchhoff's Law, still requires further investigation. The correlation between the level of AI usage and students' perceptions of its benefits in learning Kirchhoff's Law at several senior high schools was investigated in this study. Using an exploratory sequential mixed methods design, this study involved 250 students as quantitative respondents. They were divided into two groups based on their physics exam scores. One respondent represents the group that has a minimum of 80 points. Certainly, one respondent represents above or equal to more than 80 points. The questionnaire instrument was verified by two experts in the subject matter and educational technology. Quantitative results indicate that students' assessment of AI usage falls into the excellent category with an average indicator score of four. The groups with scores less than or equal to 80 tend to use AI more frequently and experience its benefits directly. Meanwhile, the groups with scores greater than 80 appear to have more experience in AI usage. Spearman's correlation analysis indicated a significant relationship between the frequency of AI usage and its preferences for the students. Qualitative results show that AI usage accelerates students' conceptual understanding of physics material, but they still have limitations in explaining complex Physics formulas. Overall, this research concludes that AI usage shows good potential in assisting the learning process of Kirchhoff's Law.

TI Development of A STEM-Integrated Guided Inquiry E-Module on Global
   Warming to Enhance Students' Conceptual Understanding
SO JURNAL PENDIDIKAN FISIKA INDONESIA-INDONESIAN JOURNAL OF PHYSICS
   EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE STEM-education; guided inquiry; e-module development; conceptual
   understanding; global warming
AB This study developed a Guided Inquiry-Based Electronic Module (E-Module) on Global Warming integrated with STEM to enhance students' conceptual understanding. This is a design-based research with three stages: introduction, prototyping, and assessment. The Plomp model was used for development. The third stage involved high school students in Indonesia. The E-Module was rated Highly Valid with an overall Aiken score of V, indicating excellent content and construct validity. The practicality test was rated highly practical by both teachers and students, meaning it was easy to use and understand. The quasi-experimental findings demonstrated significant improvements in conceptual understanding with large effect sizes. This reduced misunderstandings and promoted correct understanding. Results showed that the experimental group performed significantly better than the control group, indicating that the intervention was effective in promoting conceptual change. This study offers an empirical foundation for the synergistic integration of guided inquiry-based learning and STEM education through a digital platform. Once validated, this framework allows for the use of this approach to address complex scientific concepts and demonstrates its utility in educational contexts.

TI Effective Teaching and Assessment Tools According to Gen-Z Learners: A
   Survey Based Study in Physics Education in Nagpur India
SO JURNAL PENDIDIKAN FISIKA INDONESIA-INDONESIAN JOURNAL OF PHYSICS
   EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE cognitive; effective assessment; effective teaching; Gen-Z
AB This paper presents methodologies derived from a comprehensive survey of students studying at different levels of the education system, as well as of educators in Physics. The survey aimed to understand Generation Z's expectations from education systems and integrate their perspectives into effective teaching and assessment strategies. Key findings reveal the need for innovative approaches to enhance cognitive learning. The paper also aims to offer a list of pedagogies in accordance with Bloom's taxonomy levels. These strategies prioritize student-centered learning, interactive engagement, and personalized feedback. By incorporating Generation Z's perceptions, educators can foster a more inclusive and effective learning environment, ultimately enriching the educational experience for the next generation of students. The survey highlights a strong shift toward competency-based, skill-oriented learning in line with the National Education Policy and global trends. Students increasingly value application and problem-solving over rote memorization, resonating with Bloom's revised taxonomy. This underscores the need for formative, competency-based assessments aligned with real-world skills. While traditional classroom note-taking remains important, diverse and flexible learning resources are equally essential to meet varied learning preferences. The findings discussed in the paper offer valuable insights for educators seeking to modernize teaching practices and improve student outcomes.

TI The Effectiveness of Special Relativity Student Worksheet Assisted by
   The Pythagorean Theorem in Physics Learning
SO JURNAL PENDIDIKAN FISIKA INDONESIA-INDONESIAN JOURNAL OF PHYSICS
   EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE effectiveness; mathematical ability; student worksheet; special
   relativity of the Pythagorean theorem
AB In the 21st-century education era, integrating innovative learning media is essential to develop mathematical thinking skills and improve overall student learning outcomes, especially when addressing highly abstract physics topics such as Einstein's special theory of relativity. This research aims to implement a specifically designed Student Worksheet (SW) assisted by the Pythagoras theorem to develop mathematical thinking indicators, enhance student learning performance, and evaluate student responses toward the media. The research employed a pre-experimental method with a one-group pretest-posttest design conducted at SMAN Mumbulsari during the 2024/2025 academic year. Using convenience sampling, 72 eleventh-grade students from two physics elective classes were selected as research subjects. Data collection was carried out using validated pretest-posttest essay questions, Student Worksheets focused on four key mathematical thinking elements: specializing, generalizing, conjecturing, and convincing, and response questionnaires based on a Likert scale. Data analysis utilized the Normalized Gain (N-gain) score to measure the improvement in learning outcomes and descriptive statistics to determine the percentage of student responses. The results indicated that students' mathematical thinking skills fell into the good to very good range across all indicators. Furthermore, learning outcomes showed an average N-gain of 0.57, placing the improvement in the moderate category, complemented by a positive student response rate of 68.20%. These findings demonstrate that the Pythagoras-assisted SW effectively improves learning performance in physics. This research provides significant practical benefits as an innovative instructional alternative for physics teachers, simplifying complex, abstract concepts through a geometric approach, thereby helping students overcome mathematical barriers and fostering a deeper understanding of physics.

AB The students have had problems in forming a proper understanding of the concept of elasticity in terms of integrating numbers, graphs, and mathematics in understanding the relationship between force and deformation. This study was designed to investigate the effect of IoT-based real-time representation on the conceptual understanding of elasticity. A quasi-experimental design was used by taking a non-equivalent control group from eleventh graders. While the experimental group went through an IoT-based practicum in which they were able to visualize real-time numerical and graphical representations, the control group followed the standard practice in the laboratory. The test of conceptual understanding of the students involved the use of a diagnostic reasoning instrument, and the analysis of covariance was applied in analyzing the gathered data. The results showed that the use of IoTbased representation improved students' conceptual understanding of elasticity more than traditional classroom learning.

TI Leadership Lives in the Middle Ground Between "Best Practices Fit All"
   and "Context Is Everything"
SO RESEARCH IN EDUCATIONAL ADMINISTRATION & LEADERSHIP
LA English
DT Article
DE best practices fit all; context is everything; contingencytheory;
   situational leadership
AB This letter examines a long-standing tension in school leadership: the view that effective leadership rests on a generic set of practices, versus the view that leadership is contingent on context. Accountability policies, combined with an enduring human desire for certainty, have pushed leaders to search for practices that work everywhere. The contextual leadership perspective, by contrast, holds that there is no one-size-fits-all model, and the effectiveness of leadership depends on the broader context, the specific situation, the tasks at hand, and the people being led. This letter argues that navigating this tension is not a matter of choosing one side, combining both, or applying them in sequence. Instead, successful leadership is a continuous process ofinquiry and reflective practice that begins with problems in context, draws on evidence-based practices as resources, and through this process, leaders actively work to improve and transform their contexts. The letter also identifies five misconceptions that get in the way of this understanding.

TI The Adaptation of a Community-Engaged Intervention for Families of
   Autistic Young Adults-An Application of the Design-Based Implementation
   Research Approach
SO EDUCATION AND TRAINING IN AUTISM AND DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITIES
LA English
DT Article
DE autism spectrum disorder; family psychoeducation; transition;
   implementation
ID ADOLESCENTS; CHILDREN; OUTCOMES; QUALITY; SCALE; MODEL
AB Autistic transition-age young adults (TAY; 18-26) and their families often encounter fragmented adult services following high school exit. Caregivers frequently assume primary advocacy roles yet report high strain and limited guidance. Guided by Design-Based Implementation Research (DBIR), this study adapted and piloted Transitioning Together (TT), an evidence-based family psychoeducation program, for local implementation. Phase 1 involved stakeholder-informed service gaps and adaptation of TT to create Spartan Transitioning Together (STT), expanding eligibility to age 26 and incorporating housing, community engagement, lifelong learning, self-care, and localized resources. Phase 2 piloted STT with nine caregivers across two cohorts. Implementation outcomes, caregiver clinical outcomes, and parent-reported transition engagement were assessed using pre-post measures and effect sizes. Attendance and retention were 100%, satisfaction was high (M = 4.57-4.82/5), and fidelity exceeded 90%. All caregiver clinical outcomes improved with large effect sizes (d = 0.80-3.27). Significant improvements were observed in employment, independent living, leisure, and communication activities, with smaller gains in college preparation and service engagement.

TI Modeling digital competence in education: A bifactor-ESEM approach to
   general and domain-specific skills
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ASSESSMENT TOOLS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Digital competence; Bifactor-ESEM; Educational policy; Measurement
   invariance; Domain-specific skills
ID GOODNESS-OF-FIT; INDEXES
AB Across European and Western Balkan countries, a persistent misalignment remains between graduates' digital skill levels and the rapidly evolving demands of the contemporary workforce. Addressing this gap requires evidence-based interventions grounded in multidimensional and psychometrically rigorous assessments of digital competence. This study applies a bifactor exploratory structural equation modeling (B-ESEM) framework to evaluate university students' functional digital skills using items from the Youth Digital Skills Indicator. The model integrates a general digital competence factor with four domain-specific dimensions, capturing both shared and unique variance across skill areas. Using data from 603 students, results indicate a strong general digital competence factor alongside meaningful domain-specific contributions. The model demonstrates full measurement invariance across gender and shows predictive validity for technology affinity and digital self-efficacy. These findings underscore the relevance of conceptualizing digital competence as both transversal and domain-sensitive when informing curriculum design and educational policy. The study provides a validated and flexible measurement framework that can guide future research and targeted digital skill enhancement initiatives

TI Analysis of pre-service teachers' perception of the zoo as an
   educational space
SO REVISTA EUREKA SOBRE ENSENANZA Y DIVULGACION DE LAS CIENCIAS
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Wildlife learning; Pre-service teacher; Perception; Zoo
ID ATTITUDES; IMPACT; BIODIVERSITY
AB This paper analyzes preservice teachers' perceptions of the zoo as an educational space, evaluating the impact of three conditions: a visit to the Zoo Aquarium of Madrid, a replica of this visit at the Faculty of Education of the Complutense University of Madrid with the same zoo educator, and a control group without intervention. A quasi-experimental design was applied with pretest and posttest measures, independent groups, and purposive sampling, using a Likert-type scale validated by experts (alpha = 0.946), which covered four dimensions: content, competencies, attitudes, and a miscellany of items. The results show that both the visit to the zoo and its replica at the faculty significantly improved preservice teachers' perceptions, especially regarding the learning of wildlife content and environmental competencies. The zoo group also improved in conservationist attitudes, although, unlike the faculty group, the only attitude of reluctance to go with the student persisted, despite the improvement in their overall perception. Compared to the control group, both experimental groups showed significantly more positive perceptions about the learning of content and attitudes related to wildlife. There were no significant differences based on the teacher's high school diploma. It is concluded that participating in educational activities at the zoo can improve teachers' perceptions of the zoo. The willingness to go with students to the zoo was always positive, with 94% (faculty), 87.5% (zoo) and 56% (control), respectively.

TI Exploring Pre-service Elementary Teachers' Motivational Manifestations
   in ChatGPT-Assisted Lesson Planning: A Self-Determination Theory
   Perspective
SO ASIA-PACIFIC SCIENCE EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Self-determination theory (SDT); ChatGPT; science lesson plan;
   pre-service elementary teachers
ID THINKING
AB This study explored how pre-service elementary teachers experienced selfdetermination while designing science lessons with ChatGPT. Drawing on selfdetermination theory, it examined how the three basic psychological needs of autonomy, competence, and relatedness were manifested in ChatGPT-assisted instructional design. Six participants engaged in a 4-week project involving science lesson planning, microteaching, and reflective journaling. Data sources included lesson plans, ChatGPT interaction logs, reflective journals, and semi-structured interviews. The findings revealed that autonomy was expressed when participants critically evaluated and adapted ChatGPT-generated content, competence was fostered through iterative lesson revisions and metacognitive reflection, and relatedness emerged through peer collaboration and dialogic feedback. Rather than replacing teachers' professional agency, ChatGPT acted as a scaffold that supported motivation, decision-making, and professional growth. This study highlights the importance of framing generative AI as a tool for critical engagement in teacher education and suggests pathways for integrating AI in ways that uphold reflective practice and collaborative agency.

AB This study explored how pre-service elementary teachers understood interest in science and reflected on it through episodic accounts of past learning experiences. AB This study examines the effects of a fine particulate matter education program using digital tools and devices on elementary school students' environmental competence. Using a quasi-experimental mixed-methods design with 85 sixth-graders in Seoul, South Korea, the study compared an experimental group against a control group over 6 weeks. AB This study examined energy education in Korea's national curricula through an analysis of energy-related content in the 2015 and 2022 Revised National Curricula. Using content analysis, a conceptual framework was developed that organized energy education into four domains: energy concepts, energy resources, energy systems, and energy-related issues and solutions. A comparative analysis showed that although the 2022 curriculum placed greater emphasis on energy-related issues and solutions, disciplinary disconnections persisted. Science subjects have primarily addressed scientific energy concepts but have given limited attention to energy justice, whereas social studies subjects have emphasized sociopolitical aspects of energy while largely omitting underlying scientific principles. This separation is further illustrated by the ambiguous use of the Korean term eneoji jeonhwan, which has been interpreted differently across subjects. Overall, the findings demonstrated the fragmented nature of energy education across disciplines and underscored the need for intentional interdisciplinary integration that connects scientific foundations with societal implications.

TI International Science Education Research by Mainland China-Affiliated
   Scholars, 2001-2024: a Bibliometric Review of Publication Trends,
   Citation Impact, and Thematic Evolution
SO ASIA-PACIFIC SCIENCE EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE science education research; science education globalization;
   bibliometric analysis; Mainland China
ID SCIENTIFIC CREATIVITY; SIMULATION; GLOBALIZATION
AB The globalization of science education has increased the need to understand how research communities in diverse linguistic and educational contexts contribute to international scholarship. This study examines the development of international science education research by mainland China-affiliated scholars from 2001 to 2024. Using metadata from 559 Web of Science-indexed articles and the bibliometrix R package, the study analyzed publication trends, citation impact, journal sources, international collaboration, and thematic evolution. Findings identified three broad phases of development: fluctuating growth from 2001 to 2017, steady growth from 2018 to 2022, and rapid growth from 2023 to 2024. Across these phases, recurring and emerging themes included scientific creativity, scientific inquiry, STEM education, technology-supported learning, assessment, and higher-order thinking. Findings provide insight into how international science education research by mainland China-affiliated scholars has developed within English-mediated global knowledge networks and may inform future studies of science education research in other expanding-circle contexts.

TI Use of hands-on classroom experiments as physical analogies in student
   discussion
SO PHYSICAL REVIEW PHYSICS EDUCATION RESEARCH
LA English
DT Article
ID SPACETIME; EARTH
AB Models are commonly used in astronomy education to help students understand and discuss difficult or abstract concepts. From a physics education research perspective, metaphors and analogies are often used to support reasoning about abstract phenomena. This study investigates how students draw on classroom experiments as physical analogies (a multimodal instance of conceptual metaphor) when reasoning about exoplanetary atmospheres. We conducted two lessons: one about cloud formation on Earth and exoplanets and another about lightning on Earth and exoplanets, both including a hands-on experiment related to the topic. The students were then split into peer-led focus groups and tasked with discussing the experiment and its relation to weather in planetary atmospheres. We audio-recorded these group discussions and extracted relevant excerpts. We analyzed these excerpts sequentially using thematic analysis, network analysis, and conceptual blend analysis. We identified four input spaces used by students (relevant physics, the experiment, Earth conditions, and exoplanet conditions) and three ways in which students use analogies (mapping between domains, identifying limitations, and extending the analogy). Across these analyses, we found that students integrate these input spaces to construct blend spaces that mediate their reasoning about processes and concepts in Earth and exoplanetary weather phenomena. We also discuss implications for future research and teaching.

TI Network analysis of qualitative results from a national survey: Impact
   of outreach on physics student development
SO PHYSICAL REVIEW PHYSICS EDUCATION RESEARCH
LA English
DT Article
ID IDENTITY DEVELOPMENT; PARTICIPATION; COMMUNITIES; UNIVERSITY
AB Student experiences in physics beyond the classroom and their role in supporting student development have been the subject of increasing research attention in recent years. Results, typically from small studies at single institutions, have illustrated that facilitating informal physics experiences for nonscientists can enhance student disciplinary identity, learning, sense of belonging, and career skills. However, it is essential to examine whether these impacts are the sole provenance of institutions with well-developed outreach programs or if they may be shared by institutions anywhere. This work reports on the analysis and findings of responses to three open-ended questions presented to students who indicated they had engaged in facilitating outreach programs as part of a national survey distributed through the Society of Physics Students network in spring 2023. Employing a network analysis with Girvan-Newman clusters revealed six core themes of student experiences: community participation, resilience, transformation, audience dialogue, disciplinary development, and disciplinary connectedness. The first four of these clusters were observed to be highly interconnected, providing evidence that the impacts and experiences within them are interrelated with other clusters, particularly interactions with the audience, which is a central feature of informal physics programs. In particular, student experiences highlighted that facilitating informal physics programs enhanced their resilience and belonging, grew their physics identity, provided opportunities to develop essential career skills, and cultivated a growth mindset.

TI Academic Performance, Originality Indicators, and Student Reflections in
   an AI-Mediated Service-Learning Context in Initial Teacher Education
SO REMIE-MULTIDISCIPLINARY JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL RESEARCH
LA English
DT Article
DE AI literacy; service-learning; teacher education; academic performance;
   academic integrity
AB This study examines an AI-integrated service-learning experience in initial teacher education in which 161 undergraduate students designed educational games for real school cases. Artificial intelligence was explicitly integrated into the design process. A mixed-methods approach was adopted. Quantitative data were drawn from final project grades and Turnitin text-similarity reports; qualitative data comprised documentary analysis of students' written reflections on their AI use throughout the project. Results show high overall academic performance. Turnitin indicators revealed that most projects contained no AI-generated text, while a minority exceeded the threshold for project suspension under the assessment criteria. These results contribute to the growing empirical literature on AI integration in teacher education and point to the need for sustained instructional scaffolding to develop critical AI literacy.

AB In this paper, the effect of Leadership style and multicultural learning environment of secondary schools in three different Arab countries (the UAE, Oman and Iraq) on determining cultural identity and global citizenship for the students are examined. TI Shaping Future Principals: National Programme Leaders on Governance and
   Practice in Sweden's National Principal Training Programme
SO RESEARCH IN EDUCATIONAL ADMINISTRATION & LEADERSHIP
LA English
DT Article
DE governance; policy; enactment; principals; principal training;
   sense-making
ID SCHOOL; CONTEXT
AB The Swedish National Principal Training Programme (NPTP) plays a central role in shaping principals' roles and competencies in a rapidly changing educational landscape. This study aims to examine how the National Principal Training Programme Leaders (NPTP Leaders) navigate, understand, and lead a well-established principal training programme. Drawing on theories connected to enactment and sensemaking, seven NPTP Leaders were interviewed to explore their perspectives on the principal's role and mission, the NPTP today and in the future, and their leadership responsibilities. The study concludes that while the NPTP prepares principals for their roles, there is potential for greater collaboration and policy engagement among NPTP Leaders. Strengthening their influence within the governance framework could enhance the programme's adaptability to future educational challenges.

TI Online Scenario-Based Training to Strengthen Principals' Moral
   Leadership in School Governance: Multi-Site Evidence from Indonesia
SO RESEARCH IN EDUCATIONAL ADMINISTRATION & LEADERSHIP
LA English
DT Article
DE anti-corruption; educational leadership; ethics training; scenario-based
   learning; school governance
ID DISENGAGEMENT; PROGRAM
AB Integrity risks in Indonesian schools remain high in BOS budgeting, procurement, and transparency, eroding public trust and complicating principals' decisions. This study designs and evaluates an online scenario-based learning (O-SBL) moral-leadership model focused on school-governance dilemmas involving BOS procedures, vendor relations, conflicts of interest, documentation, and stakeholder disclosure. Using a multi-site quasi-experimental pretest-posttest design, 90 principals completed two core modules followed by four weeks of micro-scenarios. We conclude that O-SBL, combining authentic cases, structured reflection, and a common feedback rubric, substantially strengthens principals' moral-leadership competencies across diverse contexts. The model is ready for integration into principal certification and continuing professional development, particularly to enhance BOS transparency, procurement fairness, and stakeholder accountability.

TI Principals' Instructional Leadership and Teachers' Classroom Practices:
   A Mixed-Methods Study in Ethiopian Rural and Urban Schools
SO RESEARCH IN EDUCATIONAL ADMINISTRATION & LEADERSHIP
LA English
DT Article
DE instructional leadership; urban-rural divide; contextual constraints;
   adaptive leadership; dchool climate; student academic achievement
AB Effective instructional leadership is crucial for improving student achievement, yet its implementation varies significantly across contexts, particularly in managing instructional programs. This sequential explanatory mixed-methods study examines how urban-rural context shapes principals' instructional leadership in Ethiopia's Gedeo Zone, where Grade 12 national examination pass rates have declined from 18.5 percent to 0.2 percent, consistently falling below national averages. Survey data from 180 teachers reveal a significant disparity: urban principals demonstrate stronger instructional managing program, including supervising teaching, coordinating curriculum, and monitoring progress, compared to rural counterparts (p=.022). Critically, the expected relationship between principals' instructional leadership and teachers' classroom practices holds in urban schools (rho=.337, p=.001) but disappears in rural schools (rho=.160, p=.147), signaling systemic breakdown. Qualitative data from nine principals and 54 teachers across focus group reveal the mechanisms behind quantitative findings: rural principals face a triad of interconnected barriers, including overwhelming administrative burdens, severe resource scarcity, and a profoundly demoralized, unstable teaching force, which render conventional instructional leadership impossible. Confronted with these constraints, effective rural principals strategically redirect their energy toward promoting school climate through shared struggle, familial support, and symbolic community recognition. This contextually intelligent adaptation sustains teacher commitment where technical solutions fail. Findings demand fundamental policy reorientation: support systems must validate climate-focused leadership and dismantle structural barriers rather than imposing standardized blueprints ill-suited to rural realities.

TI Impact of Place-Based Climate Education on Science Attitude and Identity
SO REVISTA EUREKA SOBRE ENSENANZA Y DIVULGACION DE LAS CIENCIAS
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Climate Change Education; Climate Justice; Place-Based Education;
   Science Identity; Underserved Youth
ID CRITICAL PEDAGOGY; TECHNOLOGY; SCHOOL; WOMEN
AB This study evaluates the impact of a place-based climate education program on the science attitude and identity of underrepresented secondary students in Mexico. Using a mixed methods pre-post design with 93 students, data were collected via the S-SSAS survey and focus groups to investigate changes in student perceptions were investigated. Results indicate significant increase in both overall attitude and science identity. TI Transformations of pedagogical content knowledge in the teaching of
   Kepler's laws: the case of a professional learning community
SO REVISTA EUREKA SOBRE ENSENANZA Y DIVULGACION DE LAS CIENCIAS
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Pedagogical Content Knowledge; Professional Learning Community; Physics
   Teaching; School Astrophysics
ID SCIENCE; TEACHERS; AGREEMENT; PCK
AB This article presents a qualitative case study that analyzes the Pedagogical Content Knowledge of a physics teacher in the teaching of Kepler's laws, within the context of her sustained participation in an interdisciplinary Professional Learning Community. Based on a semi-structured interview grounded in the Content Representation framework, 41 units of meaning were identified and analyzed through open coding and emergent categories. Independent coding by three researchers yielded an initial agreement of 71% and an average Cohen's kappa of 0.78, indicating high interpretive consistency. The findings reveal a shift from algorithmic and decontextualized instruction toward more inquiry-oriented and contextualized practices supported by the use of real data, as well as the emergence of a category related to the Nature of Science that broadens this knowledge in its topic-specific dimension. The study provides qualitative evidence of the formative potential of interdisciplinary professional learning communities to support processes of Pedagogical Content Knowledge reorganization in the teaching of Kepler's laws, without establishing causal relationships.

TI What can we learn from children's science communication on YouTube?
   Mediation strategies and digital culture in science education
SO REVISTA EUREKA SOBRE ENSENANZA Y DIVULGACION DE LAS CIENCIAS
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Science communication; Digital culture; Early childhood education;
   Science education; Scientific literacy
AB This study analyzes, through a documentary design and content analysis, the communicative, didactic, and methodological strategies present in ten widely disseminated children's science communication channels on YouTube. The corpus comprised 100 videos, corresponding to the ten most viewed videos from each channel, selected up to June 2025. The analytical procedure was based on a codebook with operational definitions, observable indicators, and decision rules, applied to seven dimensions: scientific narrative, hands-on experimentation, playfulness and humor, multimodal visualization, microlearning, interdisciplinarity, and the valuing of error. The findings reveal regularities in the forms of audiovisual mediation used by these channels, characterized by the articulation of narrative structures, visual resources that support understanding, thematic segmentation, practical demonstrations with accessible materials, and engagement strategies based on humor, challenge, and the explicit recognition of error as part of the process. These results make it possible to propose criteria that may inspire teachers to adapt some of these communicative and didactic strategies in the design of their own science teaching practices.

TI Evaluation of the design of an inquiry-modeling sequence on

DE Preliminary assessment; Photosynthesis; Inquiry-based teaching;

ID LEARNING DESIGN; SCIENCE; HISTORY
AB In Design-Based Research, when evaluating an instructional proposal, the focus is usually placed on the outcomes after implementation, overlooking the importance of analyzing the design process itself. Likewise, one of the major challenges in educational research lies in the operationalization of the design process of Teaching and Learning Sequences (TLSs). In this article, we present the evaluation of a TLS collectively designed by the research group Sensociencia, analyzing the design decisions made individually by each designer through the contextual, conceptual, epistemological, and didactic dimensions. TI Didactic Treatment of the Emotional Profiles of Prospective Teachers
   When Learning the Sun-Earth System through MB!
SO REVISTA EUREKA SOBRE ENSENANZA Y DIVULGACION DE LAS CIENCIAS
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Emotional Profiles; Clusters; Primary School Teachers in Training; MBI
   teaching approach; Sun-Earth Model
AB The increasing attention to students' emotions in science learning highlights the need for a didactic perspective that emphasises their relevance and usefulness for improving science education. This study aims to expand the description of pre-service teachers' emotional responses during a self-reflective activity in which they identified the emotions experienced at each stage of an inquiry and modelling sequence on daytime astronomy. In initial teacher education, the didactic approach to emotions involves a dual perspective: self-reflection on one's own emotions while learning and consideration of their potential contribution to future teaching practice. The results reveal distinct emotional profiles after engaging in an inquiry sequence on daylight hours compared with a modelling sequence on the Sun-Earth system. The most clearly identifiable profile-both for researchers and for participants themselves- was a minority one characterised by high insecurity. However, this may be the most noticeable for teachers, while other profiles, marked by higher levels of satisfaction or confidence (inquiry) or greater concentration (modelling), may remain less apparent. The contrasting features of these profiles appear to be linked to the epistemological differences between inquiry (descriptive) and modelling (explanatory) sequences, offering valuable insights into the emotional impact of both approaches.

TI Between the ecological and the sociopolitical: challenges for teacher
   professional development in environmental citizenship
SO REVISTA EUREKA SOBRE ENSENANZA Y DIVULGACION DE LAS CIENCIAS
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Teacher professional development; Environmental education; Design-based
   research; Model
ID EDUCATION
AB Environmental Citizenship Education (ECE), understood as civic empowerment for socio-political action and the resolution of socio-environmental problems, constitutes a central axis in science education. Nevertheless, the lack of specific teacher professional development programmes hinders its integration into pedagogical practices. As part of the initial phase of a Design-Based Research (DBR) study, this research examines the training needs of 53 teachers in ECE within the Portuguese educational context. A structured questionnaire was administered across three dimensions (characterisation, needs, and preferences), validated by experts, and the resulting data were subjected to mixed and content analysis. The analysis reveals a fundamental dissonance between teachers' aspiration towards an ECE with a socio-political dimension and a practice frequently confined to a traditional ecological model. This gap may be explained by conceptual uncertainty and a lack of a repertoire of practices to promote activism and community action. Teachers express a clear preference for active methodologies and flexible formats. It is concluded that an effective professional development programme should be designed to overcome this dissonance by articulating critical foundations with participatory methodologies that enable teachers to engage in civic action.

TI Scientific education: a key component in the development of

DT Article

ID SCIENCE-EDUCATION
AB In a context of unprecedented environmental challenges, it is crucial to foster an education that goes beyond the mere transmission of knowledge, promoting a critical and interdisciplinary understanding of the relationship between society and nature. Incorporating the study of socio-environmental issues into science education leads toward a curriculum transformation that is sensitive to these challenges. The current Spanish curriculum integrates sustainability across the curriculum, acknowledging the importance of environmental education in shaping responsible citizens committed to their environment, from a competency-based perspective. This article uses the current European sustainability competence framework, GreenComp, to analyse the presence of sustainability competences in the Spanish primary education curriculum, more specifically in the area of science education. However, the results also highlight the need to respond to a model of science education that considers values and the capacity to imagine sustainable futures. The article concludes by acknowledging the opportunities provided by the current legislative context to incorporate sustainability into science education, while also emphasizing the need to do so in an interdisciplinary and transformative manner.

TI Core ideas of technology: beyond the relationship between science and
   technology
SO REVISTA EUREKA SOBRE ENSENANZA Y DIVULGACION DE LAS CIENCIAS
LA English
DT Article
DE Engineering education; STEM education; Technology education; Core ideas
AB Technology education has undergone significant transformation in recent decades, moving beyond the subordinate role outlined by the Science-Technology-Society (STS) framework to gain greater autonomy and establish stronger connections with engineering education. Despite these advances, there remains a lack of robust didactic frameworks that clearly define both the content to be taught and its appropriate structuring within compulsory education. This paper addresses this gap through an analysis of key theoretical approaches to technological knowledge. Building on this review, we propose an ontological three-level framework for classifying the core ideas of technology: (1) resources and natural phenomena; (2) processes and devices; and (3) useful applications. This model aims to provide a coherent structure to facilitate its didactical transposition in primary and secondary education. Furthermore, it seeks to lay the groundwork for developing learning progressions that guide students from concrete to abstract understanding, fostering propositional, practical, and explanatory knowledge, and thereby strengthening scientific-technological literacy from a disciplinary perspective. We conclude that identifying and establishing these core ideas is essential for consolidating the identity of technology education and for designing educational experiences that meaningfully integrate science, technology, and engineering without compromising the specificity of each discipline.

TI Progression of the Model on Biological Evolution in Secondary lessons
SO REVISTA EUREKA SOBRE ENSENANZA Y DIVULGACION DE LAS CIENCIAS
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Evolution; Models; Didactics of Geology; Compulsory Secondary Education
ID TEACHING EVOLUTION; SCIENCE; TEACHERS; LEARN; IDEAS
AB Various scientific practices contribute to the construction of school scientific knowledge. The present study analyses modelling, applied in a didactic intervention on the theory of evolution in 4 degrees de ESO. Modelling proves especially useful for the matter addressed, allowing for the description, explanation, or prediction of phenomena that are otherwise difficult to approach, such as the characteristics of living organisms (or their fossil remains) or adaptive traits. This study presents several examples of models expressed by students. It begins with the initial models' students use to describe and explain facts or phenomena, progressing toward more complex and scientifically coherent final models. Both initial and final models were categorized into different levels of complexity (from 1 to 5) to facilitate the analysis of students' conceptual progression. Most students demonstrated an improvement of one or even two levels in their final models, indicating their ability to show improvement through model-based representations. Furthermore, the analysis of model progression has proven effective in evaluating the development of other elements in students' understanding, such as miss conceptions, which were significantly reduced in the final models.

DT Article
DE Wildlife learning; Pre-service teacher; Perception; Zoo
ID ATTITUDES; IMPACT; BIODIVERSITY
AB This paper analyzes preservice teachers' perceptions of the zoo as an educational space, evaluating the impact of three conditions: a visit to the Zoo Aquarium of Madrid, a replica of this visit at the Faculty of Education of the Complutense University of Madrid with the same zoo educator, and a control group without intervention. A quasi-experimental design was applied with pretest and posttest measures, independent groups, and purposive sampling, using a Likert-type scale validated by experts (alpha = 0.946), which covered four dimensions: content, competencies, attitudes, and a miscellany of items. The results show that both the visit to the zoo and its replica at the faculty significantly improved preservice teachers' perceptions, especially regarding the learning of wildlife content and environmental competencies. The zoo group also improved in conservationist attitudes, although, unlike the faculty group, the only attitude of reluctance to go with the student persisted, despite the improvement in their overall perception. Compared to the control group, both experimental groups showed significantly more positive perceptions about the learning of content and attitudes related to wildlife. There were no significant differences based on the teacher's high school diploma. It is concluded that participating in educational activities at the zoo can improve teachers' perceptions of the zoo. The willingness to go with students to the zoo was always positive, with 94% (faculty), 87.5% (zoo) and 56% (control), respectively.

TI LEVELING UP OR LEVELING DOWN? THE IMPACT OF GENERATIVE AI ON STUDENT
   PERFORMANCE IN BUSINESS SCHOOLS
SO ACADEMY OF MANAGEMENT LEARNING & EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
AB This study investigates how generative AI (GenAI) access impacts student performance in ill-defined, time-pressured business school exams. Through an embedded mixed-methods design combining an experimental study with qualitative interviews, we identify an equalizing effect: low performers improve while high performers decline, resulting in performance convergence. Our qualitative analysis reveals the mechanism driving this convergence- GenAI-induced cognitive load inversion. Low performers experience cognitive load relief by copying chatbot output, thus bypassing the analytical work the task requires. High performers experience cognitive load amplification, struggling to process voluminous output under time pressure, disrupting their analytical processes. We argue that task structure shapes GenAI's effects in time-constrained situations: the ill-defined nature of our task elicits different cognitive challenges compared to well-defined tasks of prior research, helping reconcile mixed findings on GenAI's democratizing effects. Furthermore, the findings reveal how traditional assessments fail when GenAI masks performance differences.

TI ENGLISHIZATION BEYOND THE GLOBAL NORTH: DEPENDENCY, STRUGGLE, AND
   RESISTANCE IN BRAZILIAN MANAGEMENT RESEARCH
SO ACADEMY OF MANAGEMENT LEARNING & EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
ID DECOLONIZING MANAGEMENT; ORGANIZATION; LANGUAGE; IDENTITY
AB This paper advances understanding of Englishization in management research by addressing a key limitation in the existing literature: its predominant focus on the Global North, especially Europe. Drawing on dependency theory and postcolonial theory, we examine how management academics experience and navigate Englishization in Brazil. Based on qualitative research, we found that Brazilian academics, like their European counterparts, faced growing pressures to publish in international journals, effectively compelling publication in English, though such expectations were largely concentrated in elite institutions. We also found that Brazilian journals themselves increasingly adopted English in pursuit of international visibility, thereby intensifying pressure to publish in English and extending Englishization beyond the elite. One consequence was the publication of "Frankenstein" papers-the result of limited English proficiency and financial constraints-which paradoxically risked undermining the visibility Brazilian journals sought to enhance. Yet Englishization was not passively accepted: it was actively negotiated through strategic compliance, postcolonial ambivalence, and counter-hegemonic resistance. These findings contribute to a more nuanced, context-sensitive, and theoretically-informed understanding of Englishization by applying postcolonial and dependency perspectives to highlight its uneven trajectory across and within national contexts and to show how it is entangled with enduring Global North-South inequalities.

TI MANAGEMENT EDUCATION AS MODERNIZATION: THE HISTORICAL ROLE OF
   MODERNIZING ELITES
SO ACADEMY OF MANAGEMENT LEARNING & EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
ID INDIA
AB In extant historiography, management education was exported by U.S. elites, particularly its philanthropic foundations, leading business schools, and academic experts and consultants, to the Global South in the mid-20th century. This Americanization of management education was part of the wider Cold War-era development and was motivated by the U.S. fight against communism and the drive to promote capitalist development across the Global South. Building on and challenging this historiography, this article sets out the significant role of Indian elites and their interests in the institutionalization of management education in the country, preceding and alongside the efforts of U.S. elites. Here, management education was part of the Indian state's novel development efforts, post-independence, that fused state-led, centralized planning with capitalism and democracy, which were considered antithetical during the Cold War. The article argues that notwithstanding the significant ideological divides among the various international and national elites, it was their shared commitment to modernization that ultimately enabled the institutionalization of management education in India. The article is based on the historical efforts from 1947-1962 leading to the establishment of the Indian Institute of Management, Ahmedabad-the country's premier management research and education institution.

TI NAVIGATING PEDAGOGICAL DILEMMAS WHEN FIELDS ARE IN FLUX
SO ACADEMY OF MANAGEMENT LEARNING & EDUCATION

DT Article
ID ENTREPRENEURSHIP EDUCATION; ORGANIZATIONAL SCIENCE; COURSE DESIGN;
   MANAGEMENT; PARADOX; CULTURE; COLLABORATION; EFFECTUATION; COMMUNITIES;
   REPERTOIRE
AB Educators sit within scholarly fields, many marked by strong disciplinary boundaries or paradigms of thought. Yet, not all fields share cohesion. Fields with low paradigms have a plurality of frameworks and less consensus, which can complicate the task of course design. When low-paradigm fields confront rapid growth and are in flux, field boundaries weaken and educational mandates broaden or come into question. These conditions can generate dilemmas: opposing alternatives with distinct advantages or disadvantages but no clear path to resolution. While the lens of dilemmas has informed theories of student learning, little research has examined the pedagogical dilemmas educators face when designing courses or how they address them. We examine this question in the low paradigm, high growth field of entrepreneurship. We interviewed 27 entrepreneurship educators at a range of institutions and analyzed 86 syllabi from 84 U.S. universities (74 at business schools). We identify three pedagogical dilemmas related to learning outcomes, topic breadth, and delivery modalities. We show how educators cultivate a repertoire of strategies to navigate these dilemmas and unpack the rationales underpinning each (i.e., amplifying, retrenching, or stretching). Overall, we contribute by linking field conditions to dilemmas that emerge for educational practice, with consequences for students, educators, and the field.

TI STRONG MULTIMODALITY AND GRAPHIC ARTICLES IN MANAGEMENT LEARNING AND

DT Article

AB Our primary objective in this essay is to constructively challenge the dominant formats and templates of publishing academic articles. We argue that predominant writing conventions not only restrict epistemic inclusivity but also maintain a traditional hierarchy between the written word and visual imagery, thereby undermining the potential of combining them in composing and learning from academic articles. TI Effectiveness of support-based interventions on self-efficacy in
   patients with diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
SO HEALTH EDUCATION RESEARCH
LA English
DT Article
ID SOCIAL SUPPORT; PEER SUPPORT
AB This study conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to examine the effect of social support interventions on improving self-efficacy in patients with diabetes. A literature search was performed using Medline, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, and Embase for studies published between January 2014 and December 2023. The risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool. Effect sizes and 95% confidence intervals were calculated using R software. This systematic review and meta-analysis followed the PRISMA guidelines. From 5543 records, this research included six randomized controlled trials involving 1030 adult patients with diabetes. Social support interventions were effective in improving self-efficacy (Standardized Mean Difference = 1.33, 95% CI: 0.48-2.18) with high heterogeneity (I2 = 95%), demonstrating that social support can significantly enhance self-efficacy. This study demonstrates the impact of social support interventions on self-efficacy among diabetes patients. The findings of this systematic review strongly advocate for the prioritization and expansion of social support interventions in diabetes care, underscoring the urgent need for continued and enhanced research in this critical area (PROSPERO registration number: CRD42024566185).

TI Domain-specific approach to grit: A scale adaptation in the context of
   Turkish as a foreign language
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ASSESSMENT TOOLS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE L2 grit; Turkish as a foreign language; Scale adaptation; Criterion
   validity; Measurement invariance
ID OF-FIT INDEXES; SELF-CONFIDENCE; WILLINGNESS; ANXIETY; 2ND-LANGUAGE;
   COMMUNICATE; VALIDATION; ENJOYMENT; ENGLISH
AB This study aims to adapt and validate the L2 Grit Scale for the Turkish as a foreign language context. Data were collected from four distinct sample groups (N = 658) of university preparatory program students using a convenience sampling method. The adaptation process involved a back-translation procedure with two translators and an English Language Teaching expert, followed by a pilot test and linguistic equivalence confirmation. Validity analyses confirmed the two-factor structure through Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) (CFI = .96, RMSEA = .07, SRMR = .03) and Exploratory Structural Equation Modelling (ESEM) (CFI = .97, RMSEA = .05, SRMR = .02). Furthermore, L2 Grit emerged as a stronger predictor of willingness to communicate in Turkish (WTC) than general Grit, emphasizing its distinct role in language learning motivation. The scale's validity was further confirmed by significant correlations with foreign language enjoyment (FLE), willingness to communicate (WTC), foreign language peace of mind (FLPOM), and foreign language classroom anxiety (FLCA). Additionally, L2 Grit demonstrated a significant relationship with students' exam scores, confirming its relevance in assessing perseverance and success in language learning. Measurement invariance was established across proficiency levels and genders. Reliability analyses indicated strong internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha = .76, McDonald's omega = .77). The results demonstrate that the Turkish version of the L2 Grit Scale is a valid and reliable instrument for learners of Turkish as a foreign language.

TI Investigation of item parameter drift of anchor items in TIMSS practices
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ASSESSMENT TOOLS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Item parameter drift; TIMSS; Science assessments; Item response theory;
   Cross-national comparisons
AB This study examines item parameter drift (IPD) in eighth-grade science anchor items from the paper-based cycles of the Trends in International Mathematics and Science Study (TIMSS) in 2011, 2015, and 2019. Korea, Italy, and Saudi Arabia were selected as examples of high-, medium-, and low-achieving education systems to explore how IPD develops across different performance contexts. Using the three-parameter logistic model (3PLM) estimated in Lexter and D2 statistics computed in R, the study evaluated changes in item parameters across years and country pairs for 30 multiple-choice anchor items. The results showed that eight items exhibited temporal IPD in at least one comparison period, with most drift concentrated in the 2015-2019 and 2011-2019 contrasts. Drift occurred mainly in chemistry items at the applying cognitive level, alongside a smaller number of biology and physics items. Cross-country analyses identified 18 items with IPD in at least one country pair, with the largest number of drifting items observed between Korea and Saudi Arabia. Items involving symbolic chemical notation and representational demands were especially likely to drift across systems that differ in achievement level and opportunity to learn. These findings indicate that IPD in TIMSS science is concentrated in a subset of anchor items and is shaped jointly by temporal change and cross-national differences. The study underscores the importance of routine IPD monitoring, targeted review of repeatedly drifting items, and careful anchor selection to support valid cross-cycle and cross-national comparisons in large-scale assessments.

AB Cross-campus collaborative assessments have become an integral feature of internationalised undergraduate curricula, particularly in large, digitally mediated courses. This study explores undergraduate students' perceptions of intercultural collaboration and technical skill development in a cross-campus data analytics assessment at an Australian university. TI Gender-inclusive assessment design (GIAD): A scoping review
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ASSESSMENT TOOLS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Gender-inclusive assessment design; First-person writing; Assessment
   genre; Higher education; Transnational education
ID HIGHER-EDUCATION; UNIVERSITY; KNOWLEDGE; STYLES; VOICE; UK
AB This scoping review synthesizes scholarship on gender-inclusive assessment design (GIAD) in UK higher education and transnational education, (TNE), with a focus on authorial stance/voice, assessment genre (essay vs report), and lecturer positionality. Using a PRISMA ScR-aligned approach and a Population-Concept-Context (PCC) frame, searches of Scopus, Web of Science, and EBSCO (1998-2025) identified 504 records; 41 sources were included for analysis. Consistent with scoping review aims, no study quality appraisal or meta-analysis was undertaken. Literature consistently reports gendered discourse features in student writing (e.g., first-person usage, hedging, stance adoption) and suggests possible effects of marker expectations yet rarely translates these insights into operational assessment choices that could mitigate gendered disadvantage. Notably, it was found that no recent comparative studies evaluate performance consequences of essay vs report formats by gender, underscoring a critical evidence gap in prevalent genres. First-person permissions emerge as a plausible equity lever where third-person conventions dominate, particularly in business/management programmes. To address these gaps, the review consolidates prior work into five GIAD design levers: genre clarity and stance permissions; outcome sequencing (conclusions first vs last); first-person allowance; brief translation with structured peer feedback cycles; and transfer oriented prompts. The review offers theoretical consolidation, a methodological agenda for quasi experimental and multi-site trials, and practical quality assurance artefacts implementable within routine assurance of learning cycles across home and branch campus delivery.

TI Impact of the preparatory school's final English proficiency exam on
   students' productive skills
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ASSESSMENT TOOLS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Alternative assessment of productive skills; Washback; Error analysis;
   Low-stakes exams; Testing in tertiary education
AB This qualitative case study investigated the impact of a university preparatory school's final English proficiency exam on students' productive skills (speaking and writing) and on their emotions and opinions about learning English. 40 students and 7 instructors from a foundation university in T & uuml;rkiye participated in the study. Data were collected through students' written and spoken tasks, openended surveys, and instructors' assessment notes, and analyzed using content analysis. Findings indicate that the overall exam had more varied impacts on students than each of the specific tests for speaking and writing. The impact of the exam on students' emotions and opinions ranged from positive to negative. Among the productive skills, speaking elicited more negative emotional reactions than writing. While both speaking and writing skills were positively impacted by the exam, the effect was stronger on speaking skills, especially for students with higher proficiency levels. In contrast, no clear relationship was found between proficiency levels and the impact on writing skill. In that, higher proficiency did not correlate with greater improvement. These results suggest that the broader the exam content, the more complex its influence on learners is. The findings have implications for educators and test developers, emphasizing the importance of designing low-stakes exams that encourage positive outcomes and reduce anxiety, especially in the assessment of productive skills.

AB This study examines how student characteristics, item properties, and their interactions influence mathematics literacy using data from 7,250 Turkish students in the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) 2022.    instructional efficacy; Workload pressure; AI acceptance
ID SELF-EFFICACY; INFORMATION; SYSTEM
AB Traditional summative assessment practices in Norwegian secondary schools have faced criticism for potential biases, inconsistencies in grading reliability, and heavy workload demands on teachers, prompting interest in whether artificial intelligence (AI) can enhance fairness, objectivity, and efficiency. This study examined secondary school teachers' perceptions of AI as a tool for summative assessments and identified factors influencing their acceptance of its integration. A cross-sectional design targeted teachers from five socioeconomically and culturally diverse secondary schools in Oslo. Convenience sampling yielded 223 valid among latent variables were tested using structural equation modelling: belief in AI for assessment enhancement, digital instructional efficacy, workload/time pressure, and preference for traditional teaching methods. The results indicate a tension between progressive technological adoption and established pedagogical ideologies, suggesting that AI integration requires strategies that build teachers' digital confidence while respecting traditional practices and managing workload to avoid entrenchment in familiar methods. Limitations include the Oslo-centric sample and reliance on self-reported data; future research should incorporate longitudinal designs, qualitative methods, and broader regional representation.

   achievement in an English preparatory school
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ASSESSMENT TOOLS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Testing and assessment; Alternative assessment tools; English as a
   foreign language; Preparatory school students
AB This mixed-method research aims to investigate the impact of alternative assessment applications on the achievement scores of a group of Turkish EFL students and explore their views and feelings regarding these applications. For this purpose, a quasi-experimental design was employed. The participants were 66 preparatory class students; the experimental group included 32 and the control group 34 students. The experimental group was engaged in several different alternative assessment methods and tasks that incorporated all four language skills (i.e., reading, listening, speaking, and writing). In contrast, the control group received traditional instruction (i.e., the standard textbook exercises and worksheets as homework) in line with the policy of the school. During the process, the performances of the experimental group were assessed and evaluated formatively by means of predetermined rubrics throughout the process. On the other hand, the control group's performance was measured using conventional assessment tools such as standardized written exams, tests, and quizzes. Consequently, the quantitative data were obtained via traditional examinations, whereas qualitative data were gathered through semi-structured interviews. The quantitative data were analyzed using Multivariate Analysis of Variance (MANOVA), while qualitative data were examined through content analysis procedures. The results of the quantitative analysis indicated that the use of alternative assessment tools positively influenced the achievement scores of the experimental group and contributed to the development of their four language skills. In addition, the qualitative data revealed that the use of alternative assessment applications provided several affective and instructional benefits for the participants in the experimental group.

AB The study aimed to identify the reliability, validity, and severity of online peer grading of adult students, which remains uncertain from previous studies. Implications and recommendations are also presented in terms of academic theory and educational practice.

TI Teachers' perceptions of organizational dissent management in schools:
   Scale development and psychometric evaluation
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ASSESSMENT TOOLS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Organizational dissent management; Validity; Reliability
ID OF-FIT INDEXES; MINORITY DISSENT; VALIDITY; NUMBER; COMPONENTS;
   BEHAVIOR; SILENCE; WORK; SIZE
AB This study aimed to develop and psychometrically evaluate a scale measuring teachers' perceptions of organizational dissent management in schools. The item pool created as a result of a literature review conducted by researchers was subjected to expert evaluation for content validity. The research was carried out using a correlational research design. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses were conducted on two independent samples (n = 271; n = 223). The exploratory factor analysis supported a two-factor model consisting of 13 items, namely supportive management and suppressive management, which accounted for 59.55% of the total variance. CFA supported the two-factor structure of the organizational dissent management scale, consisting of 12 items-7 items in the suppressive management dimension and 5 items in the supportive management dimension-with excellent model fit indices. Additionally, measurement invariance across gender was examined. The changes in CFI values for the configural, metric, scalar, and strict invariance models (Delta CFI < .010) indicated that the scale functioned equivalently for male and female participants. The Differential Item Functioning (DIF) analysis based on ordinal logistic regression indicated that only two items exhibited uniform DIF with low effect sizes, while all other items functioned equivalently across gender groups, indicating that the scale generally meets measurement invariance. Furthermore, reliability analyses demonstrated high internal consistency, with Cronbach's alpha and McDonald's values ranging from .90 to .93 and Composite Reliability values between .87 and .93 for the sub-dimensions. These findings provide strong evidence for the validity, reliability, and fairness of the organizational dissent management scale.

The data obtained from 461 teachers were analyzed, and items were calibrated using Samejima's Graded Response Model. Exploratory Factor Analysis confirmed a unidimensional structure explaining 53.51% of the variance, while local independence and item-model fit were rigorously tested. The final 18-item scale demonstrated high discrimination parameters ranging from 1.815 to 4.777. The analysis of the test information function indicated that the scale provided the highest precision and reliability for teachers with collaboration levels between-3 and +1 theta. Additionally, Differential Item Functioning analysis revealed no gender bias, confirming the scale was a valid and reliable instrument.

TI Perceived Stress Scale in Romantic Relationships (PSSRR): A scale
   development study
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ASSESSMENT TOOLS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Classical test theory; Item response theory; Marriage and family
   counseling; Perceived stress; Romantic relationship;

ID DYADIC ADJUSTMENT SCALE; COUPLE BURNOUT; SHORT VERSION; QUALITY;
   SATISFACTION; MARRIAGE; SAMPLE
AB Grounded in the Systemic-Transactional Model, this study developed the Perceived Stress Scale in Romantic Relationships and evaluated its psychometric properties in adults currently involved in a romantic relationship. Using a scale development design, data were collected from two independent samples of individuals who had been in a romantic relationship. The exploratory analyses were conducted with 571 participants (age range 20-63 years), and the confirmatory analysis was conducted with 246 participants (age range 21-64 years). Construct validity was examined using exploratory factor analysis and confirmatory factor analysis. Overall, the Perceived Stress Scale in Romantic Relationships appears to be a brief, valid, and reliable measure for assessing relationship-specific perceived stress.

TI Exploring the psychometric properties of the Testwiseness Rating Scale
   using a measurement modeling approach
SO INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ASSESSMENT TOOLS IN EDUCATION

DT Article
DE Testwiseness; Psychometric properties; DIF; Rasch model; Partial credit
   model
ID TEST-TAKING STRATEGIES
AB Testwiseness refers to the ability of a test-taker or examinee to use strategic knowledge and cues within a test in order to improve their performance. These skills, cues, and knowledge are often independent of the content being assessed. Testwiseness includes skills such as using the process of elimination, recognizing patterns in answer choices, paying attention to grammatical errors, and managing time effectively. Testwiseness is important because it influences test outcomes, and potentially gives advantages to students with high testwiseness skills, rather than solely reflecting their true ability or knowledge level. Thus, understanding testwiseness is crucial for ensuring meaningful interpretation and use of test scores. The current study describes the development and psychometric evaluation of the Testwiseness Rating Scale (TWRS). We collected pilot data for the TWRS from a sample of 300 students. We evaluated the psychometric properties using a combination of factor analysis and Rasch measurement theory techniques, including differential item functioning analysis related to student gender. Overall, we found evidence to support the interpretation and use of scores from the TWRS to measure students' testwiseness. We consider the implications of our findings for research and practice and discuss directions for future research related to this instrument.

TI Bridging first-principles and semi-analytical models: a pedagogical
   approach to lattice dynamics
SO EUROPEAN JOURNAL OF PHYSICS
LA English
DT Article
DE lattice dynamics; DFT; semi-analytical models; deLaunay;
   Clark-Gazis-Wallis; BCC sodium; diamond silicon
ID BORN EFFECTIVE CHARGES; APPROXIMATION; TEMPERATURE; CONSTANTS; SODIUM;
   BASICS
AB Lattice dynamics provides a microscopic understanding of the thermal, mechanical, and transport properties of crystalline solids; however, undergraduate instruction often remains limited to simplified one-dimensional models. In this work, we present a unified and pedagogically accessible lattice-dynamical framework for real three-dimensional crystals that combines phenomenological force-constant models with first-principles density functional theory (DFT). The de Launay central-angular-force model is employed to compute the phonon dispersions of body-centered-cubic sodium, illustrating the role of lattice symmetry and the necessity of longer-range interactions, while the Clark-Gazis-Wallis three-body model is applied to diamond-structure silicon to elucidate the dominant influence of angular force constants in covalent solids. These classical treatments are benchmarked against DFT phonon calculations obtained through an open-source Python workflow based on ASE, GPAW, and Phonopy and are further validated by comparison with available neutron-scattering data. By presenting classical and ab initio phonon calculations side by side for the same materials, this study clarifies the physical meaning, applicability, and limitations of force-constant models and demonstrates how research-grade lattice-dynamical simulations can be meaningfully integrated into undergraduate instruction using accessible computational tools, enabling students to move beyond idealized textbook models toward realistic materials modeling in contemporary condensed-matter physics. This work is primarily intended for postgraduate (MSc) students, doctoral researchers, and early-career scientists in solid-state physics and materials science, aiming to bridge the gap between simplified textbook treatments of lattice dynamics and modern first-principles computational approaches.

   external force
SO EUROPEAN JOURNAL OF PHYSICS

DT Article

   systems; physics curriculum
AB We consider the optimal control problem of maximizing the energy while minimizing the external driving force for a general dissipative linear oscillator. TI Fermat's principle and image formation by stationary and uniformly
   moving spherical mirrors
SO EUROPEAN JOURNAL OF PHYSICS
LA English
DT Article
DE spherical mirror; Fermat's principle; relativistic optics; reflection
ID REFLECTION; LIGHT
AB We analyze image formation in concave spherical mirrors using Fermat's principle of stationary optical path length while treating stationary and uniformly translating mirrors within a single variational framework. Physical rays follow from imposing stationarity with respect to the reflection point on the surface, yielding a general mirror formula together with the associated law of reflection. In the paraxial limit, the Gaussian mirror equation is recovered, whereas spherical aberration is described exactly through the height dependence of the focal distance beyond the paraxial regime. Ray-tracing histograms and optical-path-length curves illustrate the clustering of rays near the paraxial image distance. The treatment is self-contained and is aimed at advanced undergraduate courses in geometrical optics and special relativity.

TI Counterintuitive mass dependence in a variable-geometry Atwood machine
SO EUROPEAN JOURNAL OF PHYSICS
LA English
DT Article
DE Atwood machine; constrained motion; nonlinear dynamics; time-dependent
   constraints
ID ORBITS
AB We investigate the dynamics of a variable-geometry Atwood machine in which the angle of the supporting rope evolves during the motion. Starting from the kinematic constraint and Newton's second law, we derive an explicit expression for the acceleration of the load and show that it depends not only on the instantaneous geometry, but also on its rate of change. A central result is the existence of a counterintuitive regime in which increasing the driving mass leads to a reduction in the upward acceleration of the load. By distinguishing between partial and total derivatives with respect to the driving mass, we demonstrate that this effect cannot arise from the explicit mass dependence of the equations of motion. Instead, it originates from the trajectory dependence introduced by the evolving geometry. Numerical simulations reveal a well-defined region where this non-monotonic behavior occurs and allow the different contributions to be identified. The analysis shows that the dominant negative contribution is associated with the sensitivity of the geometric configuration to the driving mass. This system therefore provides a clear example of how time-dependent constraints can alter the response of a mechanical system and offers a useful illustration of non-monotonic behavior in a familiar classical setting.

TI Charged particle in a magnetic field: from basic physics to Brownian
   motion
SO EUROPEAN JOURNAL OF PHYSICS
LA English
DT Article
DE charged particle dynamics; static magnetic field; Langevin equation;
   stochastic processes; angular momentum; Bohr-van Leeuwen theorem;
   physics education
ID LANGEVIN THEORY; DIAMAGNETISM
AB In university-level physics education, the motion of a charged particle in a magnetic field is typically restricted to idealized, non-viscous environments, focusing primarily on circular motion derived from the balance of magnetic and centripetal forces. This paper presents a more comprehensive approach based on Newton's equations of motion, providing deeper physical insights and allowing for generalizations to more realistic scenarios. We investigate the particle's dynamics in viscous media, accounting for Stokes friction alongside the Lorentz force, and explicitly calculate trajectories, displacements, and angular momentum. Furthermore, the framework is extended to Brownian motion using the classical Langevin equation with white thermal noise. Our findings reveal that the mean angular momentum (and consequently the magnetic moment) approaches a finite non-zero value in the long-time limit, leading to a discussion of how the results should be interpreted within the framework of classical statistical mechanics, in particular in relation to the assumptions underlying the Bohr-van Leeuwen theorem. This approach serves as an effective pedagogical tool, bridging concepts from classical mechanics, statistical physics, and stochastic processes while encouraging student debate on the foundations of classical magnetism.

   Learners: Does Proficiency Make an Impact?
